Short facts are that the pre-emptor filed Pre-emption Case No.41 of 1991 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Pirganj, Rangpur under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption against the preemptees and others stating, inter alia, that the land measuring 66 decimals of Plot No.381/628 of C,S. Khatian No.2, S.A. Khatian No.115 originally belonged to Naresh Chanara Basu and Indu Prava Basu in their raiyati right. The C.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared and finally published in their names. Before R.S. Khatian the said Naresh Chandra Basu and Indu Prava Basu after transferring the said land including the case land left for India. Md. Akbar Ali, Munsur Ali, Hosen Ali and Hosen Ali got the case land on the basis of lease. As per the deed of exchange dated 27.12.1986 Md. Akbar Ali transferred 161/2 acres of land to the pre-emptor. In this way the preemptor became a co-sharer in the disputed holding. The pre-emptor has got his homestead in the western portion of the case land. The opposite party No.3 of the pm-emption case sold the case land to the pre-emptee Nos.1 and 2 by a kabala dated 03.04.1991 beyond the knowledge of the preemptor. No notice of the kabala under pre-emption was served upon the pre-emptor. The pre-emptees are stranger purchasers in the case holding. The cause of action of the .case arose when the kabala under pre-emption was registered under section 60 of the Registration Act.

full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff, inter alia, is that Ashutosh Roy was the CS recorded tenant of the suit land along with other land under the Ex-lord Abdul Hakim Chowdhury, Ashutosh Roy while in ownership and possession died leaving two sons Kalipada Roy and Devi Pada Roy whose names were recorded in SA Khatian. Thereafter said Kalipada and Devi Pada sold out the suit property along with others to plaintiff by registered sale deed dated 11-8-1969 and delivered possession. During Revisional settlement suit property has been wrongly recorded in the name of the defendant. The plaintiff came to know about wrong recording of the suit property in the name of the defendant from the local Tahasildar on 15-6-1982. It is stated that as a result the wrong record of RS. Khatian in the name of the defendant has been a cloud cast upon the title of the plaintiff and hence plaintiff filed the suit. 

 4. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegation. The case of the defendant, inter alia, is that the suit land comprising an area of 0.50 acre in CS plot No. 279 originally belonged to Rajkhear debuttar Estate of which two brothers named Kali Pada Roy and Devi Pada Roy were joint shebaits, that one Hazrat Ali took pattan of an area measuring .04½ acre from the Estate in the first part of the year 1360 BS at an annual Jama of Rs. 9/15/0, that said Hazrat Ali while in ownership and possession of the land on regular payment of rent to the landlord sold the pattan land to the defendant by registered sale deed dated 30-4-1954 at a consideration of Taka 97.00 Only. The said Hazrat Ali also sold the rest of the pattan land to the defendant by registered sale deed dated 3-11-1954 and thus defendant became owner and possessor of 0.5½  acre of land, that the defendant has been possessing the suit land openly, peacefully and adversely for more then 12 years by mutating his name and paying rent. At about the time of taking pattan by Hazrat Ali, one Anwara Khatun also took pattan of 0.04½  acres of land where she had homestead and she sold a portion out of her pattan land to one Shamsuddin and said vendor had possession of the land and as such, they were necessary parties in the suit, that the land purchased by the defendant was wrongly recorded in the SA Khatian in the name of Kalipada and Devi Pada and for correction of record the defendant filed Miscellaneous case which was decreed ex parte on 17-4-1970 and record of right was accordingly corrected. During RS operation the suit land has been correctly recorded in the name of the defendant. Against such record that plaintiff filed dispute and objection case before the settlement Authority which were rejected on 27-2-1973 and 10-4-1978 and as such, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation, that RS Khatian has been finally published in the name of the defendant, that plaintiff has illegally and fraudulently created some deeds in respect of the entire area of the land in suit plot, that as a matter of fact plaintiff has or had no right title and possession on the suit land wherein the defendant has been in peaceful, possession, that deeds created by the plaintiff are antedated, and forged and that the suit is liable to be dismissed.

full_judgment:
2. Defendants are the appellants Plaintiff respondent filed Title Suit No. 66 of 1966 if the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court, Serajganj for declaration of title and recovery of possession. His case was that the suit land described in the schedule Ka and Kha of the plaint appertaining to Khatian Nos. 123 and 125 respectively of mouza Bhangari originally belonged to landlords Girija Sannyal and Aswini Kumar Sannayal. Basarat Akanda and Maidan Akanda used to cultivate the suit land in raiyati right as tenants paying half of the produce as rent. Maidan Akanda surrendered his land in favour of the landlords who in turn gave that land in borga to Bassarat Akand. Bassarat Akanda died leaving two sons namely Mofiz Akanda and Mahim Akanda who by inheritance got the land of Khatian No. 123 of Schedule 'Ka' as raiyati tenant at a rental of half of the produce and also possessed the land of Khatian No. 125 of Schedule Kha in borga like, their father. Having difficulties in paying rent in crop Mafiz and Mahim prayed to the landlords for conversion of Khatian No. 123 into money rent and further prayed for leasing out the land of Khatian 125 to them by fixing a jama. Narayan Chandra Roy, Manager of the Estate leased out 3.91 acres of land of Khatian Nos. 123 and 125 to the plaintiff Mofiz and Mohim at a rental of Rs. 15/8/- annas on 15th Chaitra, 1348 B.S. after receiving Nazarana and issued a Likhon in favour of Mahim and Mofiz who had been possessing the land as tenant on payment of rent to the Sanayal landlords. The present provisional rent Roll Khatian has been finally published in the name of Mahim and Mofiz who have sold two plots out of their jote to the plaintiffs by registered kabala dated 28.1.65. His further case was that the defendants cut and took away jute grown by the plaintiffs for which the criminal case was started but the case was dismissed and being encouraged by an order of acquittal the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land on 11.6.66. 

 In that view of the matter the appeal was allowed. In Second Appeal the High Court Division on analysis of the evidence found that the plaintiff had proved the tenancy right of Mofiz and Mohim and their settlement by Ext. 3. This Ext. was not considered by the Court of appeal below in correct perspective. Ext. 3 Likhon was issued in 134.8 B.S. for the lease of the land of both the Khatians. Appellate Court below considered that there was no corroborative evidence and accordingly disbelieved this Likhon. The High Court Division rightly pointed that there was positive evidence of P.W. 3 to substantiate the genuineness of the Ext. 3. It is found to be genuine as it has been found by the trial court, the High Court Division inferred that the suit was filed within 12 years from 1363 B.S. and the same was not barred by limitation. Next the kabala Ext. 1 of the plaintiff had been admitted by both P.Ws. Mofiz and Mohim. It is clear that the lower appellate court below wrongly set aside the judgment of the Munsif inasmuch as plaintiff's title has been amply proved by the oral evidence as well whereas the appellate Court below had found the possession in favour of the defendant by saying "not known, what capacity". When a dispute is brought before the Court for adjudication, it is necessary for the Court to come to conclusion this way or the other. The defendants have got no document of title. This was noticed by the appellate Court below as well. The defendants relied on an Amalnama Ext. C and C (I) and even the appellate Court below compared the signature of Aswin Sannayal on Ext. C series with dakhilas Ext. D series and found that Ext. C series were not genuine. Notwithstanding this finding that the defendant had got no document of title yet the judgment and decree of the trial court was set aside. 

 4. Mr B.N. Chowdhury appearing for the defendant-appellant contended that the plaintiffs' vendors were mere borgadar and their tenancy could not be proved. The position of the defendants is worse. In the Khatian it is mentioned that the right of Sannyal was মধ্যস্বত্ব চিরস্থায়ী (illegible) and as such a lease holder under them would be tenant. But strangely enough in the Amalnama of the defendants Ext. C series, it shows that Korfa pattan. The trial Court concluded that the contention of the plaintiff that these were created after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act when the Sannayal became raiyat by operation of law and on a mistaken notion thought that no lease could be granted to them and therefore korfa pattan was mentioned. This position shows that Ext. C series were created for the purpose of the suit the inference drawn from such document—is a question of law and there is no escape from the conclusion that the trial court was correct in drawing the conclusion as it did. Now the question of status of the plaintiff's vendor. In the case of Abu Nasser Sayedullah Vs. Abdul Malik alias Mala and another 12 D.L.R. 206 a single Bench considered section 3(17) proviso and held that a borgadar could become a tenant before the introduction of the provision to clause (17) of section 3 but cannot be so after its introduction unless the conditions in the exception are fulfilled. The decision was doubted in 14 DLR 801 in the case of Munir Mondal and others Vs. Paramatha Nath Chowdhury and others by a Division Bench and it was held that borgadar recorded in C.S. Khatian as tenant before introduction of the provision in 1928, can plead tenancy right after the introduction of the proviso. It was observed that the interpretation given in 12 DLR would create anomalous position namely once a tenant, he could not be considered as tenant for the subsequent period. Reliance was placed on high authority, A.I.R. 1940 P.C. 124 that such construction so unreasonable and imprecise ought not to have been preferred when another construction is open. Subsequently. In the case of Krishna Chandra Paul Vs. Khoyar Sardar, 20 DLR 745 another Single Bench took the view that a person who is holding land by giving a share of the crop must be doing so under the system know as Borga, Adhi or Bhag and, if the C.S. record show that before the amendment in 1928 the person was holding the land as a permanent raiyati and the rent was fixed at half the crop and that case is included in the rent which has been fixed, then it must be held that the person was not holding the land under the system of Borga, or adhi but he was a tenant with occupancy right and the rent was fixed by which the cess was also included.

full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal, in brief, are that respondents 1-9 as petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No.27 of 2001 in the Court of District Judge, Sylhet stating facts that Hazarat Syed Shah Bahauddin (R) known as Putla Shah, one of the disciples of Hazarat Shahjalal (R) went to Vadeshwar about 700/800 years ago to preach Islam religion. At that time a mosque was constructed and a pond was excavated on the gifted land of local devoted muslims. The mosque is known as Dakshinbhag Jame Masjid. The mosque and entire properties were managed by the elderly muslims of that area and thereafter by a panchayat which was subsequently turned as a managing committee. The suit property was 0.50 acres which was recorded in the name of Masjid Managing Committee in SA Khatian 2910, plots 7624, 7625 and 7626 of Vadeshwar mouja. The managing committee maintained proceedings of the management of the mosque from 1960. Lastly in the year 1998 a committee of 11 members was formed where Syed Siddique Ullah was a member. When the above said Siddique Ullah engaged with the activities subversive to the interest of the mosque, the committee expelled him. He then filed a petition to the Administrator of Wakf (respondent 10) on 1-11-1998 for enlisting the property as waqf estate in the name of Syed Zaker and others alias Dakshinbhag Jame Masjid Wakf Estate. In the application he claimed that a wakf deed was executed on 12 Falgoon of 1289 BS by the original owners of the property. The petitioner masjid committee raised objection against the step of enlistment by filing application to the Wakf Administrator. The application for enlisting the suit property as wakf property was heard on several occasions and finally the claim of the masjid committee was rejected by the Administrator on 15-5-2001 and applicant Syed Siddique Ullah was appointed as mutawalli and his committee was approved. The petitioner then filed the aforesaid miscellaneous case under section 50 of the Ordinance, 1962 for setting aside the order passed by the Wakf Administrator. 

 5. Mr. Md. Saidur Rahman, learned Advocate for the appellant takes us through the materials on record and submits that the learned Additional District Judge failed to take into account the fact that Syed Zakir and other successors of Hazrat Syed Saha Bahauddin was the recorded owner of the property of Touzi No.3945 and Thak No.4983 and they made a deed of waqf on 12 Falgoon, 1289 BS; the SA Bujrat khatian was prepared in the name of Syed Zakir and subsequently SA Khatian 2910 was finally prepared and published in the name of Vadeshwar Dakshinbhag Jame Masjid represented by its mutawalli Syed Abdul Fatta and that the disputed property has been finally enrolled as Syed Zakir and others alias Dakshinbhag Jame Masjid Wakf Estate bearing EC No.18708 on 3-6-1999 on the basis of an application of the successors-in-interest of the estate. The Wakf Administrator correctly rejected the application of the Masjid Managing Committee on 15-5-2001 but the Additional District Judge eared in law in not taking into account the aforesaid facts and law and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is to be set-aside. The Additional District Judge travelled beyond the provision of law of section 50 of the Ordinance, 1962 and relying only on SA Khatian allowed the miscellaneous case which is required to be interfered with by this Court. He further submits that the findings and decision that the wakf deed requires to be registered under section 17 of the Registration Act is perverse because under Muslim Law wakf means a permanent dedication by a muslim and, as sueh, its registration is not mandatory. Mr. Rahman finally submits that enlistment of property as wakf estate after long lapse of execution of the deed is not barred under section 47(7) of the Ordinance, 1962. The provisions laid in the aforesaid section are not mandatory and, as such, the findings and decision of the learned Judge to that effect cannot be sustained in law. Since the Masjid Managing Committee failed to prove their claim over the disputed property they are estopped from raising any question that it is not a wakf property. The Additional District Judge ought to have rejected the miscellaneous case considering the aforesaid facts and law and by not doing so eared in law which is to be interfered with by this Court in appeal. This appeal, therefore, should be allowed and the order passed by the wakf administrator on 15-5-2001 be upheld. 

 7. We have considered the submissions of both the sides, gone through the materials before us and the provisions of law referred to by the parties. It is found from Exhibit-1 series that 0.50 acres of land of SA Khatian 2910 plots 7624, 7625 and 7626 has been recorded in the name of Masjid Managing Committee. The Committee paid rent to the concerned authority through Exhibit-2 series. Exhibit-4 series are the resolutions of the committee and Exhibit-5 series are of income and expenditure of the committee. The above documents prove that the Masjid Committee has been managing the affairs of the property from long ago. In the miscellaneous case they stated of maintaining the record of the property from 1960. We do not find anything in the record that before 1998 there was any sort of claim that the property was wakf property. In the year 1998 Siddique Ullah for the first time filed an application to the Wakf Administrator for enlistment of the property as wakf property. In enlisting the property Siddique Ullah relied on the unregistered deed dated 12 Falgoon, 1289 BS corresponding to 24-2-1883 AD.

full_judgment:
7. The case of the petitioner in short is that in schedule 1st (Ka)-1st (Chha) property Charu Gazi, Budha Gazi and Chan Gazi were the owners in equal share. The defendant Nos. 35-52 are heirs of Budha Gazi and defendant Nos. 53-117 are heirs of Chand Gazi, Charu Gazi died leaving one son Ramja, two daughters Raiman Bibi and Kulchum Bibi. Thereafter Raiman Bibi died leaving defendant Nos. 12-31 as here heirs. Kulchum Bibi died leaving one daughter Baicha Bibi and brother Ramjan Ali. Baichama Bibi died leaving defendant Nos. 32-34 as her heirs. Thus Ramjan All inherited total 2.00 acres from his father Charu Gazi and sister Kulchum Bibi .52 decimals of 2nd schedule land is the self acquired property of Ramjan Ali in whose name S.A. Khatian No. 145 was finally published for the 2nd schedule land. The Second (Ka) to second (Gha) schedule of an area of total 081 decimals of land was purchased by Ramjan Ali by his own source of money in the benami of his son Korban Ali by registered Kabala dated 25.8.1941, 25.12.1946, 28.12.1946 and 2.05.1956. Thus Ramjan Ali while had been owning and possessing 3.3. acres of land mentioned in aforesaid schedule he died leaving Korban Ali as son, Plaintiff as son of predeceased son Roushan Ali, defendants No. 6-11 as sons and daughters of predeceased daughter Buchi Bibi. In the facts and circumstances plaintiffs share is 1.33-1/5 acres as heir of Ramjan Ali and defendant Nos. 6-11 share is .66-3/5 acre as heirs of Ramjan Ali. The defendant Nos. 1-5 are heirs of Korban Ali. The defendant Nos. 6-11 have exhausted their share by selling to others. The defendant Nos. 32-34 as heirs of Kulsum Bibi through daughter Baichama Bibi having got .41½ acre by amicable settlement sold .41½ acres to the plaintiff by Kabala dated 13.9.1968 (Ext-5) which he purchased by his own fund and thus plaintiffs claimed 7 1.74-710 acres by inheritance and purchase. The plaintiff though purchased .21 acre of plot 417 from Askar Ali son of Budha Gazi, but he subsequently sold it to defendant Nos. 118-121 (Ext.6) and now plaintiff prayed for partition of his entitled share. The defendant Nos. 35-52 as heirs of Budha Gazi and defendant Nos. 53-117 as heirs of Chand Gazi will get 2/3rd shares from properties of 1st (Ka) -1st (Chha) only. Earlier petitioner filed partition suit No. 78 of 1968 which was decree in preliminary and then infinal form, but was set aside at the instance of Korban Ali and his two sons defendant Nos. 1 and 2. 

 9. The Opposite party No. 14 as defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying he material facts of the plant stating inter alia that Charu Gazi died leaving one son Ramjan Ali and two daughters namely, Raiman alias Nabijan Bibi and Kulsum Bibi. In respect of 1st (Kha) schedule property Ramjan Ali was the Korfa tenant in whose name 35 No. C.R. record was finallyp8ubished. That Raiman Bibi alias Nabija Bibi died leaving one son Noab Ali and daughter Chali Bibi and then Chali Bibi died leaving two daughters namely Jobeda and Abeda and brother Noab Ali Jobeda (defendant No. 31) sold 10 decimals out of 1st (Ka), 1st (Kha) and 1st (Uma) to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by Kabala dated 17.3.1976. That Abeda died issue less leaving sister Jobeda who gifted 20 decimals of land out of the 1st (Ka) 1st (Kha) and 1st  (Uma) properties in favour of defendants Nos. 1 and 2 by registered gift deed dated 17.11.1990. That Noab Ali died leaving wife Buchi Bibi defendant No. 17, three sons defendant Nos. 18, 19 and Sundar Ali (the predecessor of defendant Nos. 20-26) and four daughters who were defendant Nos. 27-30 and the aforesaid sons and three daughters (defendant Nos. 28-30) transferred 18 decimals of land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by registered kabalas dated 20.03.1976 and 40 decimals of land by registered Kabala dated 17.11.1990 out of their share in suit 1st (Ka),  (Kha), (Ga) and (Uma) properties. That Kulsum Bibi (sister of Ramjan Ali) died leaving one son Basat Ali and one daughter Baichama Bibi and then Baichama Bibi died issue less leaving husband Altab Ali and brother Basat Ali and then Altab Ali remarried to have given birth of defendant Nos. 32-34 who have no share in the property left by I3achama Bibi and then Basat Ali died leaving defendant Nos. 12-13. That the properties of suit 1st (Uma) and (Cha) schedule rightly recorded in C.R. Khatain No. 15 and 19 in the names of Chan Gazi, Budha Gazi and Ramjan Ali and Omisssion of names of Raiman and Kulsum (Sisters of Ramjan Ali) did not affect their right, title and interest in the said properties. That the properties of suit 1st (Ga) was recorded in the name of Chan Gazi in C.R. No. 11 and 1st (Gila) and (Cha) in the name of Budha Gazi in C.R. Nos. 5 and 18. That the 1st (kha) schedule property was recorded in the name of Ramjan Ali in Khatain No. 35 as Korfa Tenant and Ramjan Ali purchased nor them 21 decimals of plot No. 417 of 1st (Ka) schedule in the benami of his grad son plaintiff by kabala dated 18.06.1947 that in addition to that Ramjan Ali also purchased 23 decimals of plot No. 519, under Khatain No. 117, 14 decimals of plot 329/2 under Khatian No. 329/2 and 47 decimals of plot 212 under Khatain No. 9 and 52 decimals of 2nd schedule in the benami of the plaintiff of 2nd schedule it he benami of the plaintiff Ramjan Ali in total had been owner of 2.31833 acres and then died leaving son Korban Ali, Predecessed son of plaintiff and predecessed daughter's sons daughters defendant Nos. 6-11. Then Korban Ali died leaving two sons who are defendant Nos. 1 and 2, three daughters who are defendant Nos. 3-5 and in the facts and circumstances plaintiff has claimed more than his entitled share and therefore prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 10. The defendant No. 35 (ka) Abdul Latif and defendant No. 47 Saheb Ali (heirs of Budha Gazi) herein opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed a joint written statement denying the material facts of the plaint stating inter alia that it is false story that in story that in the 1st (ka) 1st (cha) schedule lands the three brothers Charu Gazi, Chand Gazi and Budha Gazi were owners of equal share. Their predecessor Goda Gazi was owner in 2.1 acres of 1st (ka) schedule, in 2.69 acres in 1st (Umma) schedule, in .84 acres in 1st (Cha) schedule and .13 acres in 3rd schedule total in 5.67 acres of land which devolved upon the said three sons equally after death of Goda Gazi before Chakal Roushanabad Survery. Thereafter the three brothers separated their mess construing separate houses for them and during their separate living Chand Gazi purchased the 1st (Ga) schedule land by his own found for which C.R. Khatian No. 11 was prepared in his name for 1.45 acre. Similarly Budha Gazi Purchasd schecule (Gha) and 1st (Cha) total of an area of 2.03 acres by his own money for his own benefit for which C.R. Khatian Nos. 5 and 18 had been prepared in his sole name, while Charu Gazi and Chand Gazi were in separate mess, they jointly took korfa settlement of 51 decimals of 1st (kha) schedule land on condition to pay specific amount of paddy to owner Budha Gazi and under the above facts and circumstances Charu Gazi died leaving one son Ramjan Ali and two daughters before C.R. operation and Chan Gazi waived his right in joint Korfa tenancy and thereafter Ramjan Ali alone cultivated the 1st (Kha) schedule land as Korfa tenant and in his name C.R. Khatian No. 35 was published, but subsequently he surrendered the land in favour of the owner Budha Gazi who re-settled the said land with Lal Mia as Korfa tenant and while Lal Mia was possessing the said land rent receivers interest was abolished and then in S. A. Khatian No. 146 the said land was recorded in the name of heirs of Lal Mia and in the facts and circumstances the 1st (Kha) schedule was liable to be struck of from the plaint. Their further case is that Kulsum Bibi (the daughter of Charu Gaii) died leaving son. Basat Ali and daughter Baichama and then Baichama died leaving brother Basat Ali and husband Aftab Ali. Thereafter Aftab remarried giving birth to defendant Nos. 32-34 and Basat Ali died leaving defendant Nos. 12-16 is his heirs. 

 The defendant Nos. 55-64 (heirs of Chand Gazi) herein opposite party Nos. 66-75 contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material facts of the plaint stating inter alia that the 1st (Ga) schedule land of an area 1045 acres was the self acquired property of Chand Gazi in whose name C.R. Khatian No. 11 was published and the defendant Nos. 53/55-127 are his heirs. That the heirs of Budha Gazi, i. e. the defendant Nos. 35-52 are the exclusive owners in 1st (Gha) and (Cha) schedule land in addition to their 1/3rd share in 1st (ka), 1st (Uma), 1st (Cha) and 3rd schedule land. That in his 1/3rd share within 1st (Ka) 1st (Uma), (Cha) and 3rd schedule property Chand Gazi got 1.89 acres and he acquired 1.45 acres of 1st (Ga) schedule. Then he died leaving three sons and three daughters namely; Jonab Ali, Arab Ali, Noab Ali; Nurjahan Bibi, Nekjan Bibi, Elemjan Bibi. The present defendant Nos. 55-64 are the successive heirs of Jonab Ali who claims. 75 -13/18 acres in their share. 

 13. It is admitted by the parties that the 3rd schedule land appertaining to C. R. Khatian No. 15 is ejmali pond and therefore the 3rd schedule pond remained nonpartiable ejmali property. 

 16. Mr. Md. Abdul Kader Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners both the Civil Revisions takes me into the application and other materials on record and submits that the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendant admittedly are the members of same joint family of some joint family the land occupied by their predecessor jointly and thereby there are entitled to get equal share in all the Khatain including the land mentioned in the plaint as schedule first Ga, Gha and Cha and this material fact were correctly found by the trial Court but the court of appeal below without considering this legal as well as material aspect came to finding that the Khatian No. 11, 5 and 18 which were related with their said schedule land were not the owner of the petitioner only to incorporate the name of the predecessor of the defendant which are misreading and non-consideration of the definition of joint family as such it committed an error of law and occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the land of schedule 1Ka, Uma and Cha was obtained by the plaintiff petitioner by way of inheritance and got his share with the other predecessor of the defendant No. 2 and other defendants namely Chant Gazi, Buda Gazi but Chant Gazi and Buda Gazi neither claimed the land of the said schedule first Ga, Gha and Cha neither in the life time nor even the defendant claimed the said land in the earlier suit of partition nor even it was claimed in execution of the solenama but the court of appeal below totally failed to consider this material as well as legal aspect and committed an error of law in his decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 18. Mr. Mubarak Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite parties in Civil Revision No. 3480 of 2004 takes me into the court of appeal below and submits that since the name of the predecessor of the defendant namely Buda Gazi, Chant Gazi being the owner of the land and their names have correctly recorded in the Khatian has found by the court of appeal below thereby it did not commit any error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. As such, he prays to make the Rule in respect of Civil Revision No. 3480 may be discharged. 

 19. Heard the learned Advocate for both the sides, perused the said application and other materials on record. 20. It appears from the record that the petitioner as plaintiff has filed the suit for partition in respect of 1.74-7/10 acres of land on the allegation that the schedule land of the schedule first Ka-Cha originally belonged by three brothers namely Charu Gazi, Buda Gazi and Chand Gazi and they obtained the said land while they were jointly living in a same mess and after that date the plaintiff got the said land by way of inheritance. It was further alleged that the plaintiff got the land of schedule No. 2 by way of purchased separate sets of defendant contested the suit by filing separate suit by filing separate written statement and denying the material allegation of the plaintiff but admitted that the predecessor Charu Gazi, Buda Gazi and Chand Gazi as joint family members till operation of khatian has mentioned in the schedule first Ka-Cha and also admitted the purchased land of the predecessor in schedule 2. 

 23. So, the trial Court after considering the plaintiff and defendant witnesses got the finding that the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendant namely Charu Gazi, Buda Gazi and Chand Gazi were living jointly in a same mess and they got equal share in respect of the land of the schedule 1' (Ka), Uma and Cha. Subsequently the claim by the defendant No. 2 that the land in question of schedule I St Ga and Gha and Cha obtained by Chand Gazi and Buda Gazi by their own interest with their own fund for the said land. In support of such claim there is no piece of documentary nor any oral evidence to prove the said fact of his statement. Even the said fact was not disclosed in the earliest point of time of suit as well as in the solenama rather it was admitted that said three brothers Chand Gazi, Buda Gazi Charu Gazi were living together in same mess jointly. It appears that the trial Court on consideration of the materials on record including the records in the khatian itself got the finding to the effect that: 

 24. To justify the said finding about the joint ownership of the said 03 brothers .by the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court, I have carefully perused the evidences-on-record along with the said finding of both the courts below, the trial court found that the defendant witness No. 2 corroborated and admitted the plaintiff's case that Charu Gazi, Buda Gazi and Chand Gazi were living on the same mess and during their joint family the names of the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendants were recorded in the khatians as mentioned in first schedule No. 1 Ka, l Uma and 1 Cha in equal share. On perusal the said khatian along with deposition of PWs and D. W. 2 it appears that the said finding of the trial Court is correct and based on material-on-record. But there is no basis to incorporate the name of the predecessor of the defendant in the subsequent khatian. It further appears that the trial Court gave explanation and reasons in his finding. Even the defendant No. 2 did not disclose the said fact in the earlier suit of partition as well as in course of execution of the solenama between the parties as evident from Exhibit-10. Non discloser the said fact of the defence plea in the earliest point of time and subsequent discloser such fact without any valid reasons are not free from principle of subsequent embellishment by the defendants for their interest. On perusal it appears that the finding of the Court of trial based on materials-on-record with cogent reasons as mentioned above. Whereas, the finding of the Court of appeal below in respect of first schedule No. 1 Ga, 1 Gha and 1 Cha are without any basis as such the same has no legal in the eye of law. As such only incorporated the name of the predecessors of the defendant in the subsequent khatian does not create any title neither in favour of their predecessors nor in favour of the defendants in any way and while the predecessor of the defendant namely Charu Gazi and Buda Gazi admittedly were the members of joint family with Chand Gazi. Thereby the incorporate of the name of the Chand Gazi and Buda Gazi in Khatian No. 5, 11 and 18 have no legal basis and as such no title has been passed by such wrong records of right in favour of the defendants. Therefore the finding of the lower appellate Court to that effect is baseless as well as misreading and non-consideration of the materials-on- record as mentioned above thereby it has committed an error in his decision and thereby occasioning failure of justice.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party no.1 herein as plaintiff instituted Civil Suit no.61 of 1996 impleading the opposite party nos.2-6 as defendants for declaration of title. Plaintiff's case in short is that the suit land originally belonged to C.S. recordee Bhagirathi Das who sold the suit land including other lands to Sree Kamini Kumar Chakraborty. Sree Subodh Debnath, Sreemoti Sailabala Debi by three separate deeds all dated 15.03.1954. Accordingly S.A. Khatian recorded in their names. Said Subodh Debnath and others sold out the same to Abdul Rahman Bepari by deed dated 21.07.1970. Abdul Rahman Bepari sold the suit land measuring .07½ sataks including other lands to Md. Habibullah and Most. Jahanara vide two registered deed dated 11.08.1975. Abdul Rahman sold and handed over exclusive possession of the land of suit S.A. Plot no.476 corresponding to latest Settlement Plot no.410 to the purchasers by the aforesaid deed. Abdul Rahman sold out other lands apart from suit land by sale deed no.629 and 630 dated 26.01.1976 to other persons and in the said deeds though S.A. Plot no.476 corresponding to latest Settlement plot no.410 written but actually they have been in possession of .38 sataks land which are not suit land. Abdul Rahman Bepari, Md. Habibullah and Jahanara Begun sold out their purchased land to Most. Amena Khatun by registered deed dated 20.11.1976 who transferred the land in favour of the plaintiff by Heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 16.08.1990. Thus the plaintiff acquired absolute right, title and interest in the suit land by deed of Heba-bil-ewaj dated 16„08.1990. Plaintiff came to know from the office of the Assistant Commissioner (land) on 10.11.1995 that .51 Sataks of land of R.S. Plot no.410 under R.S. Khatian no.49 has been recorded in the name of Sreenagar Thana Parishad. Said wrong and illegal entry of record creates cloud upon the title of the plaintiff. Hence, the present suit. 

 4. The case of the defendant nos.1-5 is that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and the suit is liable to be dismissed for want of cause auction. Further contending that the suit land is the Government khas land and the S.A. recorded owner did not transfer the same to any person. Abdul Rahman Bepari created a false deed dated 21.07.1970 and R.S. Khatian for .15 Sataks of land wrongly recorded in the name of Abdul Rahman Bepari who had no legal right to transfer the suit land. They prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 5. The Case of the defendant nos.6 and 7 is that the land in C.S. Plot no.476 under C.S. khatian no.242 including other lands belonged to Bhagirathi Das who sold out the same to Kamini Kumar Chakraborty, Sree Subodh Kumar Chakraborty and Sreemoti Amia Bala Debi vide sale deed dated 20.11.1945 and delivered possession thereof. S.A. Khatian finally recorded in the name of Sudhir Kumer Chakraborty for 6(six) annas, Subodh Chandra Debnath for 4(four) annas and Sremoti Sailabala Debi for 6(six) annas and they in their turn sold out the suit land including other lands to Abdul Rahman by registered deed dated 21.07.1970 and delivered possession thereof. R.S. Khatian has been finally published in the name of Abdul Rahman and he in his turn sold out .38 sataks of suit land vide deed no.629 and 630 dated 26.01.1976 to Abdul Latif Laskar who died leaving one son Abdul Majid Laskar, two minor daughters namely Salma Khatun and Shahnaj Begum and wife Most. Masuda Khatun as heirs. The heirs of said Abdul Latif Laskar sold out their inherited property to Narayan Chandra Saha and Madhab Chandra Saha vide registered deed dated 30.05.1985. Said Narayan Chandra Saha and Madhab Chandra Saha jointly sold out .38 Sakats suit land to A. Majid and A. Sattar vide registered deed dated 01.07.1985. A. Majid died leaving 2(two) sons namely Md. Monir Hossain and Md. Panir Hossain and wife Ripana Akter who in their turn sold out the land to Sheikh Dalil, Most. Angura Begum, Sheikh Khalil and Most. Bedana Begum vide deed dated 17.04.1995 who also in their turn sold out .38 sataks of land to the added defendant nos.6 and 7 vide deed dated 17.05.1998 and delivered possession thereof. 'Thus the defendant nos.6-7 acquired absolute right, title and interest in the suit land of .38 Sataks and are in peaceful possession beyond the statutory period of limitation. Record in the name of Thana Parishad in wrong, in-operative and ineffective. Plaintiff's case is false, concocted and fabricated and the plaintiff was never in possession of the suit land. With such averments they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 14. Upon threadbare discussions on the issues the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit holding that the vendor of the plaintiff Amena Khatun purchased the suit land from Jahanara Begum, Habibullah and Abdul Rahman by registered deed dated 20.11.1976 and said Amena Khatun transferred the suit land in favour of the plaintiff vide Heba-bil-ewaj dated 16.08.1990 which are proved by Exhibit-7, 8, 10 and 11. From Exhibit-"Kha-and "Kha(1)" produced by the added defendant nos.6-7 it is apparent that in the deed nos.629 and 630 dated 26.01.1976 the quantum of land is .38 sataks in S.A. Plot no.476 and on the north of the suit land the possessor is Gunjar Ali. But on perusal of S.A. Khatian no.242 it appears that the quantum of land in S.A. Plot no.476 is 66 sataks and on the north of the land the possessor is Razzab Ali and as such by the said deeds the suit land was not transferred in favour of the added defendants because the quantum of land in S.A. Plot no.476 is not 38 sataks. But total land sold by the deed nos.629 and 630 is .38 sataks and on the north the possessor is Gunjar Ali. The added defendants also produced DCR and one rent receipt marked as Exhibit 'ka' and 'ka-1' which also shows that the quantum of land in S.A. Plot no.476 is .38 sataks. It is not mentioned in the Exhibits .38 sataks out of 66 sataks. Thus the Trial Court held that the suit land was not transferred by the deeds no.629 and 630 dated 26.01.105. The Trial Court also discussed the evidence of the P.Ws. and D.Ws. P.W. I stated in his deposition that Amena Khatun purchased the suit land from Jahanara, Habibullah and Abdul Rahman vide deed dated 20.11.1976 and since then the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land on behalf of her daughter Amena Khatun. After purchase of the suit land Amena Khatun paid rents to the Government exchequer in the name of Sudhir Chandra Deb Nath and thereafter Amena Khatun transferred the suit land in favour of her father i.e. the present plaintiff by Heba-bil-ewaj dated 16.08.1990. This P.W. also stated that .51 Sataks of their land recorded as .53 Sataks in the name of Thana Parishad which is wrong and illegal. P.W.1 was cross-examined by added defendant nos.6-7 but failed to shaken her. The trial court also examined the defendants' witnesses. D.W.1 stated in his cross-examination that " আমি উত্তর পাশ দিয়া নালিশী জমি দাবী করিয়াছি।" He stated that in the south of his land the plaintiff is cultivating his land. He also stated that he does not aware whether the plaintiff is a land owner or borgadar. D. Ws. 2, 3 and 4 stated in their deposition that on a tree besides the suit land a signboard is hanging in the name of Siddiqur Rahman. D.W.5 stated in his deposition that in a tree besides the suit land a signboard carrying the names of Siddiqur and Siraj is hanging. By discussing the oral and documentary evidence the trial court arrived at a finding that the plaintiff has been able' to prove his case and thus decreed the suit. On perusal of the judgment passed by the appellate court below, it appears that the learned Additional District Judge after re-assessing the evidence on record independently dis-allowed the appeal and thus affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. It also appears that the Additional District Judge on perusal of the Exhibits-7, 8, 10 and 11 arrived at a finding that the plaintiff-respondent is in possession of the suit land. He also assessed the exhibit- "Kha" and "Kha(1)" produced by the added defendant appellants along with S.A. Khatian no.242 wherein the quantum of land mentioned against S.A. Plot no.476 is 66 sataks and on the north the possessor is Razzab Ali. But in the deeds i.e. Exhibit `kha' and `kha-1' the quantum of land is .38 sataks and on the north the possessor is Gunjar AIi Thus the appellate court below also arrived at a finding that by Exhibit `kha' and 'kha-1', the suit land was not transferred in favour of defendants no.6 and 7.

8. Mr Hasan Foez Siddique with Mr Nurul Islam Matubber and Mr Munshi Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsels appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners, submits at the very outset that the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court mainly on 3 grounds. 1. The plaintiffs did not bring all the properties and the schedule of Hotchpot. 2. There are several parties in the jote jointly owning and possessing the suit land but they were not made parties, as such, the suit is bad for defect of parties and 3. There are tanks situated in Khatian Nos. 202 and 291 and there are as many as 200 shares in those tanks who were not made parties. The learned appellate Court observed in his judgment that the plaintiff ought to have sought joint possession but the plaintiff did not seek joint possession in the tank in assailing the judgment of the appellate Court. The learned Counsel further submits that this is nothing but a misreading by the learned Additional District Judge and Bankruptcy Court, Chittagong but, as a matter of fact, the plaintiff sought joint possession in the tanks and drew attention of the Court. The learned Counsel next submits that the properties of Khatian Nos. 202, 291 and 256 were not brought into Hotchpot as because the properties were not disputed, as such, plaintiff did not feel any necessity to bring those properties in the schedule of Hotchpot. There is no legal bar and no suit can fail by reason merely on non-joinder of parties under Order I, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He also submits that the law is also relaxable in a suit for partition that all the joint property should be included in the schedule of properties. The learned Counsel, in support of his contention, relied in the case of Safaruddin vs Fazlul Hug reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151. The learned Counsel finally submits that the lower appellate Court without considering and without applying his judicial mind reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court which is not at all sustainable in law because in the suit for partition the defect of parties and hotchpotch of the partition suit will not defeat the suit. This is a mere technical defect for which the suit will not be defeated. In this connection the learned Counsel referred the case of Rabija Khatun vs Badshah Meah reported in 47 DLR (AD) 511 wherein it has been stated: 

 "Hotchpotch—Rule of equity—In a case where all the joint properties were not brought into hotchpotch of the partition suit, the omission will not defeat the suit—a rule of equity as opposed to a rule of law shall be applied on the convenience of the parties concerned without causing prejudice to anyone". 

 10. On the other hand, Dr Rafiqur Rahman with Mr Abdus Salam Mamun and Mr Md Shahiduzzaman, the learned Counsels appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant-opposite parties, at the very outset submits that whether in a case where the defect of parties and hotchpotch of the schedule of the properties is present a simple partition suit is maintainable or not. Next he submits that the learned trial Court is absolutely wrong and erroneous in determining the necessary parties of a partition suit as well as the joint properties of all the co-sharers in a partition suit and came to a wrong and fallacious finding occasioning failure of justice. The trial Court, without considering the legal implication of a partition suit and without considering the effect of defect of parties and hotchpotch of the schedule in a partition suit, decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff which is manifestly perverse. The learned Counsel in support of his contention referred the case of Nurul Afsar vs Rafiqul Ahmed reported in 51 DLR (AD) 155 wherein it has been held: 

 "Hotchpotch—If properties are left out in a partition suit it brooks further litigation. It is true that this rule is relaxable. But there are specific situations calling for relaxation." 

 11. He further submits that the properties of Khatian No. 291 Plot No. 109, the properties of Khatian No. 202 Plot Nos. 124, 125 and 131 and also properties of Khatian No. 256 Plot No. 147 were not brought into hotchpotch and not even in the schedule of the suit properties. He also submits that the plaintiffs sought for Saham of 44 decimal of land in the first schedule as per 1/3 share of his predecessor but, as a matter of fact, as per 1/3 shares the plaintiffs were supposed to get 22 decimals of the suit properties but the trial Court, without calculating the quantum of land merely on the basis of surmise and claim of the plaintiffs, gave Saham of 44 decimals of land and passed the decree in favour of the plaintiff and thereby acted illegally which is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the lower appellate Court was absolutely right and justified in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, inasmuch as not considering the defect of parties and hotchpotch of the suit land. Although the learned Advocate for the petitioner tried to advance his argument that the properties of undisputed khatian and the co-sharer of undisputed khatian if not made parties that will not defeat the suit but, as a matter of fact, this will prejudice other co-sharers. 2. The petitioner, the pre-emptor, filed the above Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1996 for pre-emption of the case land under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 stating, inter alia, that he is a co-sharer in the case holding by inheritance; his brother, the respondent No. 2, by a sale deed dated 17.06.95 transferred the case land to the pre-emptee, the respondent No.1, a stranger to the case holding; on notice about the above sale dated 17.6.95 not being served upon the pre-emptor he was totally ignorant of the transfer till 27.10.96; the respondent No. 2 by sale deed dated 22.6.1996 having sold some other land of the case holding to the above pre-emptee he filed Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1996 wherein the pre-emptee, on 27.10.1996, filed written objection disclosing therein the earlier transfer to him by sale deed dated 17.06.95 and then only he, for the first time, came to know about the above sale deed dated 17.06.95; he then after obtaining the certified copy. of the said deed filed the case seeking pre-emption, although in the above sale deed dated 17.6.95 the khatian number has been shown as 160, actually it would be Khatian No. 13. The pre-emptee-respondent no.1 contested the pre-emption case by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that he purchased the case land from the respondent No.2 for construction of his residence and he went into possession of the case land on 18.06.95 and he then raised dwelling house thereon at the cost of Tk.25,000/- and that the pre-emptor is no longer a co-sharer in the case holding. 

 "In the light of discussion made above I may conclude that the alleged R.S. Khatian No. 160 was finally published on 6.05.98 i.e. long after the transfer of the case land to O.P. No. 1 i.e. at the time of transfer of even at the time of entry in volume of the case land is in law a part of S.A. plot No. 40 of S.A. Khatian No. 13. In law it cannot be said that the case land was a part of R.S. plot No. 88 or R.S. Khatian No. 160, and it was splitted up from the S.A. Khatian No. 13. So I can conclude at the time of transfer of the case land the petitioner appellant was a co-sharer by dint of holding. According to section 2(13) "Holding" means parcel or parcels of land or an undivided share thereof held by reiyat or an under rayat from the subject of separate tenancy. 

 Moreover in perusing the S.A. map adduced by the appellant it is seen that S.A. plot No. 40 is a compact plot. The further contention of the appellant is that he is a co-sharer by purchase in the case jama by purchasing 23 decimals of land plot No. 40 of khatian No. 13. The appellant has produced the original kabala dated 2.1.88 to substantiate his contention (Ext.3). In the light of discussion made above I may conclude that the appellant is co-sharer in the case jama by dint of holding and purchase as well by the kabala dated 2.01.88 and accordingly does not need to seek pre-emption of the case land as adjoining land owner. So the trial court is not at all justified in holding the view that the case is bad for defect of parties for not impleading the adjoining land owners. The record transpires that the petitioner appellant has impleaded all S.A. recorded tenants (including Aszar Ali). So I can concluded that the instant case is not bad for defect of parties. It is categorically admitted that the O.P respondent No.1 is a stranger in the case Jama."

3. The case of the plaintiffs in short is that proforma defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali, father of proforma defendant No.8 Ahmmad Ali, proforma defendant No. 10 Alamat Ali and Julmat Ali husband of proforma defendant No.9 Mohammadi Begum, acquired right, title and interest in suit CS plot No. 313 of CS Khatian No. 362 Ext. 5(a) of Mouza Barabo along with other lands on the basis of a deed of heba-bil-ewaz dated the 17th December, 1935 Ext. 1 and A executed in his favour by Jamirjan Bibi and Annabi Bibi, widow and daughter respectively of late Alef and he was in peaceful possession of the said property. While in such title and possession defendant No. 7 transferred entire area of 2.51 acres of suit plot No. 313 to Mohammad Azizur Rahman by a registered deed of sale dated 16th April, 1957 Ext 2 and delivered possession of the said land to the said purchaser. While in such title and possession the said Azizur Rahman transferred eastern half of the suit CS plot No 313 to plaintiff No. 1 Mosammat Masuma Khatoon by a sale deed dated 7th July, 1958 Ext. 2(b) showing the purchased land as Block 'B' in the Map attached to the said sale deed and the western half of the said suit plot No. 313 to plaintiff No. 2 Mosammat Rezia Khatoon by sale deed dated 7th, July, 1958 Ext. 2(a) showing the said land as Block 'A' in the Map attached, to the said sale deed and made over khas possession of said land to the said purchaser plaintiffs. Thereafter the plaintiffs got their names mutated with the Government Tahsil office and have been paying rents since 1367 BS and onwards under separate rent receipts Ext. 4 sides. The said CS plot No. 313 has been recorded in the revisional survey operation in six separate plots. As there was wrong recording in respect of the area the plaintiffs fired an application on 25.3.74 Ext. 11 before the Revenue Officer, Dhaka for correction of the said mistake. Since the date of purchase the plaintiffs remained in exclusive khas possession of the suit plot No. 313 measuring an area of 2.51 acres by growing crops therein through their cultivators and bargadars openly, peaceably, and to the knowledge of all persons including the principal defendants and their predecessors-in-interest and of independent right, free from all encumbrances for more than 17 years and by adverse possession too. 

 7. Their specific case, in short, is that one Alef was owner of 8.89 acres of land in raiyati jote right in mouza Barabo and the said Alef died leaving his widow Jamirjan Bibi and four daughters, namely, Aliman Bibi, Saliman Bibi, Kctabi Bibi and Annabi Bibi but during the CS operation the said land was recorded in CS Khatian No. 362 Ext. 5(a) wrongly in the name of Jamirjan Bibi alone. Jamirjan Bibi and Annabi Bibi created a Heba-bil-ewaz deed on 17.12.1935 Ext. 1 & A in respect of 3.43 acres of land of CS plot No. 313, 365 and 341 in favour of defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali son of Aliman Bibi. Saliman Bibi also created a Kabala dated 9.2.49 Ext B in respect of 2.60 acres of land of CS plot Nos. 313, 365 and 371 in favour of said Kadam AIi Sirajbi Bibi daughter of Ketabi Bibi sold .73 acre of land out of CS plot No. 313,365 and 371 to Ahmed Ali, Julmat Ali and Alamat Ali defendant Nos. 8 to 10 sons of Kadam Ali by sale deed dated 19.5.47 Ext. B(I) and delivered possession of the same then and there from CS plot No. 313 as per amicable arrangement Sirajbi Bibi by amicable arrangement with other co-sharers had been possessing 1.14 acres of land from the western side of CS plot No. 313 and defendant Nos. 8 to 10 were given possession out of Sirajbi Bibi's 1.14 acres of land from western side of that plot. Kadam Ali had been possessing 1.37 acres of CS plot No. 313 from the eastern side of that plot and he transferred some of his lands to Azizur Rahman who also transferred the same to the plaintiffs. The names of Jamirjan Bibi, Kadam Ali, Ahmed Ali, Julmat Ali, Almat Ali and the plaintiffs were recorded in SA Khatian No. 365 Ext. C(1). Julmat AIi died leaving defendant No.9 Mohammadi Begum and his father defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali as his heirs. Defendant Nos. 8 and 10 sold 0.30 acres of land from CS plot No. 313 to the defendant Nos. 1 to 4 by a registered kabala dated 27.7.76 Ext B(2) and delivered possession of the same then and there with their already constructed thatched hut. Defendant No.9 also sold .06 acres of land from said CS plot No. 313 to the defendant Nos. 5 and 6 by a sale deed dated 27.7.76 Ext. B(3) and delivered possession of the same to those purchasers then and there. Thus the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 are in possession of 0.36 acres of land and the defendant Nos. 8 to 10 are in possession of 0.37 acres and the plaintiffs are in possession of 1.37 acres and Sirajbi Bibi is in possession of 0.41 acres of CS plot No. 313 but the present RS record has not been properly prepared and the same is under dispute. The 'A' Schedule property of the plaint is ejmali property of the plaintiffs and the defendants as well as Sirajbi Bibi and as such plaintiffs' suit for declaration of title in the said land and recovery of khas possession from the 'B' schedule land which is part of the 'A' schedule land is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. The learned Advocate for the appellants submitted that the land described in 'B' schedule of the plaint is vague and indefinite and on this ground alone plaintiffs' prayer for recovery of possession is liable to be dismissed. He further submitted that Sirajbi Bibi is an admitted co-sharer of the suit holding and on the basis of purchase from her in the year 1947 defendant Nos. 8 and 10 and their brother Julmat Ali became a co-sharer in the suit plot and by purchase from them the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 also became co-sharers in the suit plot with the plaintiffs. As such court below was not justified in declaring title of the suit 'A' schedule property in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs having failed to prove dispossession and the defendants being in possession on the basis of their purchase as well as entry in the SA Khatian they could not be evicted from the suit land. 

 10. Is to the vagueness of suit property it is found from description of 'A' schedule to the plaint that the entire area of 2.51 acres of land of CS plot No. 313 of CS Khatian No. 362 of Mouza Barabo with boundaries has been mentioned. In the 'B' Schedule of the plaint the plaintiffs have described dispossessed 0.10 decimals of land to be lying to the west of CS plot No. 313 being the land filled up with earth having a thatched hut measuring 8x5 cubits buict thereon. The learned Advocate of the appellants contends that as there is no mention of boundary of the said decimals of land it is difficult to identify the same. The learned Advocate of the respondents in reply contends that 'though boundaries of the said 0.10 decimals of land have not been mentioned in the plaint no specific objection as to the identity of the said land was either taken in the, written statement or in the cross-examination of the PWs. On consideration of the written statement and the deposition of the witnesses we find that no such objection was taken as to the identity of the suit 'B' schedule land. Therefore we find no merit in the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants in this respect. 

 12. The appellant Nos. 1-6 have filed an application for amendment of paragraph No. 19(d) of the written statement filed by them as defendant Nos. 1-6 and also to add a new paragraph No. 19(i) in the said written statement the middle portion of the said paragraph No. 19(d) full stop after the words "as per amicable arrangement" is sought to be deleted and the words between Kadam Ali and his sons defendants 8,10 and Julmat Ali is sought to be added after the said full stop. It is also sought to be added in the new paragraph 19 if that Title Suit No. 501 of 1978 has been filed by Sirajbi Bibi in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for partition of the entire lands of CS Khatian No. 362 of mouza Barabo and subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 812 of 1985 of the Second Court of Subordinate Judge: Dhaka and the same is still pending. The learned Advocate for the respondents vehemently opposed this prayer for amendment on the ground that it is an afterthought to make their inadmissible evidence as admissible, We have already found earlier that the claim of the defendants that defendants 8, 10 and Julmat Ali got possession in their purchased land on the basis of amicable arrangement with their father Kadam Ali cannot be relied upon. Moreover, as pointed out by Mr. BK Das, the learned Advocate for the respondents that the said partition suit is no longer pending, rather it was decreed by the trial Court and on appeal by his clients the said decree was reversed by this court in First Appeal No. 843 of 1991. In view of the above, we find no merit in the said application for amendment of the written statement of defendant Nos. 1-6. Moreover, even if we allow this amendment the unamended written statement of defendant Nos.8 and 10 will remain intact in paragraph No. 19 (d) in the very same language as in paragraph No. 19 (d) of the written statement of defendant Nos. 1-6. They being mere subsequent purchasers from defendant Nos. 8 to 10 cannot make a contradictory claim with their vendors. Therefore, the application for amendment is rejected. 

 14. The learned Advocate for the appellants relied on the decision in the case Abdul Jalil Sikder and others Vs. Khorshed Ali Dakua and others reported in 27 DLR (AD) 143 and in the case of Hazera Begum and others Vs. Rousan Ara Begum and others reported in 39 DLR (AD) 22 and contended that even if the plaintiffs are found to have been in sole possession of the suit plot No. 313 that will not amount to ouster of the co-sharer defendants however long their possession might be and title of the defendants, will not be extinguished in the suit plot by such possession of the plaintiffs and as such, court below was wholly wrong in declaring title of the plaintiffs in the entire land of suit plot No. 313. It is true that defendant No. 7 Kadam Ali being a descendant of the original owner and his sons also similarly being transferees from a descendant of the original owner sole possession of Kadam Ali could not have extinguished the title of his co-sharer sons. But the plaintiffs being strangers to the family and they having purchased from Azizur Rahman transferee of Kadam Ali and having got exclusive possession to the knowledge of the defendants and having mutated and recorded their name in assertion of their title denying title of sons of Kadam Ali and paid rents from the time of their purchase continuously in spite of objection by the sons of Kadam Ali their open possession is a notorious fact and nothing but ouster of the sons of Kadam Ali from the suit plot. Even if we accept defence case that sons of Kadam Ali also possessed the suit plot with their father as deposed by PW 3 fact remains that the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the suit plot for 16 years as already found by us and this leads to the irresistible conclusion of their ouster from the suit plot. It may be noted that SA Khatian Ext. 5 prepared by merely revising the CS Khatian and recording names of sons of Kadam Alialong with the names of the plaintiffs even without omitting name of CS recorded tenant Jamirjan Bibi and the government acquired plots has no presumptive value and we find up merit in the contention of the appellants that they have interest in the suit property on the basis of the said SA Khatian. Moreover, it is pointed out by the learned Advocate for the respondents that in the judgment of FA No. 843 of 1991 between the same parties it has been found that corrected RS Khatian in respect of the suit plot was finally published in the name of the plaintiffs subsequent to the SA Khatian. Since the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the entire land of CS plot No. 313 openly, notoriously and continuously for more than 16 years beyond the statutory period of limitation, right, title and interest if any of the sons of Kadam Ali in that plot had been extinguished by adverse possession before the alleged dispossession of the plaintiffs from the 'B' schedule land. Facts of the above decisions are distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the present case and as such principle enunciated in those cases are of no help to the appellants.

parties:
Naimuddin Mondol @ Namiruddin -------Defendant No.2-Respondent-Petitioner 
vs
1. Md. Abdus Sattar ------ Plaintiff-Appellant-Opposite Party
2. Government of Bangladesh, and others ------- Defendants-Respondents-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land is the property under Khas Khatian No. 1 of the Government. In the remark column of the said khatian it has been written useable by the people and in the CS Khatian there was a remark 'eidgah' in the remark column for which the suit land had not been given on pattan. The suit property is a ditch, pond and eidgah. A mosque has been built in some portion of the suit land. The local people use the land for a long period from time immemorial. But in the RS Khatian, there was no remark in the remark column of the plot as useable by the people. Defendant Nos.1-2 on 15-12-2003, refused the easement right of the people, hence the plaintiff filed the instant suit on the consent of all for declaration of the easement right over the suit land. 

 4. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit land is the khas land of the Government. It has been recorded in the CS, SA, and RS Khatians in the name of the Government in Khas Khatian No. 1. There is no scope of building a mosque or an eidgah illegally in the suit land. 

 13. Conversely, Mr. Pirjada Syed Abu Hanifa 1bna Jamal Md. Alam the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Md Sultan Mahmud, Advocate on behalf of plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 submits that admittedly the suit land originally belonged to the Zamindar namely Shankarpur Zamindary Estate directly under the proprietorship of the Zamindari and rightly recorded in the CS Khatian' in the name of the Zamindar who dedicated the suit land to the Muslim mass people for their eidgah as well as for general use and accordingly, the said intention/dedication published in the CS Khatian in its remark column. 

 16. On the other hand, Mr. Prahlad Debnath, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, appearing for opposite party No.2-Government submits that initially the instant suit was filed by 2% of the local people as the plaintiffs but subsequently, plaintiff No. 2 withdrew himself from the suit by applying. He also submits that after filing the case a notice was published in the daily newspaper but no one came forward to add themselves as a party in the case. He further submits that the land of plot No. 5848 has been given to the defendant-petitioner by way of settlement by executing a hukumnama. He next submits that an Advocate Commissioner was appointed by the Court to inquiry the suit land physically and after physical examination, the Advocate Commissioner submitted a report before the Court opining that there was no existence of eidgah in the suit land; rather, there were dwelling houses, trees, etc. 

 18. Mr. Dutta in the course of his submissions contends that it appears that during the trial, the Trial Court decided to issue No. 2 separately in favor of the plaintiff. While the Court decided to issue Nos. 1, 3 & 4 jointly against the plaintiff. In deciding all those issues the learned Trial Judge took all the oral and documentary evidence of the contending parties including the commissioner's report and held that, at present, there is no existence of eidgah in CS and RS plot Nos. 5848 and 8419, and long before the same has been converted to the private land of defendant No. 2, who obtained the same vide Lease Order of the P.S. Case No. 1136 of 1969-70 (exhibit-'G'), Letter of Allotment of PS Case No. 1136 of 1969-70 dated 13-1-1979 (exhibit-'H'), and registered Kabuliat No. 1727 (exhibit-`1'). He mutated his name and got Khatian No. 1071 (exhibit- T), paid Government dues and got DCR (exhibit-'K'), and paid rent [exhibit- 'L'—'L(7)']. 

 23. On scrutiny of the evidence on record, it appears that admittedly, the suit land along with then Zamindar namely "Shankarpur Zamindary Estate" i.e. directly under the proprietorship of the Zamindar, and during the CS operation, their names were recorded in CS Khatian No. 1 and the same was finally published in their names and subsequently on 14-4-1956, the entire land devolved upon the Government by the cessation of zamindary system. During the SA and RS operation, the suit land along with other lands was recorded in the name of the Government in its Khas Khatian No. 1, and permanently settled the suit land in favor of the petitioner under PS Case Nos. 198/1964-65 and 1136/1969-70 respectively. The petitioner mutated his name, paying rent, and enjoying the property.

full_judgment:
3. The suit properties measuring 38.59 acres belonged to four brothers, namely, Purna Chandra Chowdhury, Rashik Chandra Chowdhury, Bama Charan Chowdhury and Sashi Kumer Chowdhury, and, the R.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared, and, finally published in their names, and, they were in possession. They verbally settled 28.9425 acres of land to their relation Sukumar Biswas @ Sukomoy Biswas, Sunil Bikash Sen, Mihir Kanti Das & Sachindra Nath Guha in the year 1940, and, the remaining ½th share measuring 9.6475 acres remained with the said original owners. The further case; is that, the names of the settlement holders Sukumar Biswas, @ Sukamoy Biswas, Sunil Bikash Sen, Mihir Xanti Das, and, Sachindra Nath Guha were recorded in the R.S. Khatian, and, while in possession, they transferred the suit land by 10 kabalas dated 22.04.1978, 03.04.1978 and 09.04.1978 measuring 9.88 acres in favour of the plaintiffs, but, the defendant Government forfeited the suit land belonging to the plaintiffs to the extent of 7.40 acres by issuing the alleged notices dated 27.01.1988 and 29.01.1987 respectively. Hence is the suit. Subsequently, defendant Not.5-11 by filing application got themselves added in the suit. 

 5. The defendant Nos.5-11 also contested the suit by filing a separate written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alias, that, the suit is not maintainable, and, the suit has got no cause of actions. The suit land originally belonged to Purna Chandra Chowdhury, Bama Charan chowdhury, Rashik Chandra Chowdhury and, Shashi Kumar Chowdhury, and, R.S. Khatian No.451 was finally prepared in their names. Thereafter, Purna Chandra died, and his 4 anas share devolved upon his son Sateyndra Bijoy Roy Chowdhury, Rasik Chandra died, and whose shares devolved on his son Upendra, Lal, and, after his death, his son Gouranga Prashad Chowdhury. The defendants stated that, R.S. recorded tenant Barra Charan Chowdhury died, and his share devolved upon his 2 sons Surendra Bijoy Chy and Tejendra Lal Chowdhury, and R.S. tenant Shashi Kumar gifted away 2.89 acres of land to his son Dhirendra Roy Chowdhury and, his brother-in-law Pranab Das on 25.06.1967. The defendants stated that, Sateyndra Roy Chowdhury and Tejendra Lal Chowdhury sold away 7.00 acres of the suit schedule land, and, other land in favour of Pranab Das dated 25.06.1967. The defendants stated that, while Pranab Das has been holding possession of the suit land for more than statutory period of limitation, he sold away the suit land to the defendant Nos.6-8 and to the extent of 3.68 acres on 12.03.1986 and on 05.03.1986 to the defendant Nos.6-8 and to others to the extent of 3.63 acres and on 12:03.1986 to the defendant No.5 and others and on 10.03.1986 to the defendant Nos.9-11 and others to the extent of 3.66 acres. The defendants stated that, after having purchased the suit land, they have been holding peaceful possession of the suit land by paying regular rent thereof. The defendants alleged that, M.R.R. Khatian No.637 was prepared wrongly in the name of Sukumar Biswas and others. The defendants denied right, title, interest and possession of the Plaintiffs in the suit land and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 12. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned, Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.1-6 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that, the plaintiffs having purchased the suit lands by registered instruments have acquired good title in the suit land, and the same is not liable to be forfeited under President's Order No.98 of 1972, and therefore, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He further submits that, the learned District Judge having found that, the impugned notices are illegal and without jurisdiction, it follows that the forfeiture of the suit land has not been Validity made, and, consequently, the acquisition of title in the land by the plaintiffs by registered instruments cannot be said to be invalid. He next submits that, the present suit relates to the declaration of title on 9.88 acres of land, which is much less than one hundred standard Bighas, and, the plaintiffs are not required to submits any statement in the prescribed form, and the lands held by the plaintiffs being not in excess of one hundred standard Bighas is not liable to be forfeited to the Government, and, so the omission of the proviso to, Article 8 of the President's Order No.98 of 1972 did not affect the title of the plaintiffs acquired by registered instruments as the land is much less than one hundred standard Bighas, and, therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division with regard to the plaintiffs' title to the suit land is sustainable in law. He finally submits that, the land being 9.88 acres not having been belonged to the previous owner after transfer to the plaintiff, the said lands not liable to be forfeited to the Government, and, as such, the High Court Division rightly passed the impugned judgment and order, and, therefore, he prays for dismissal the instant appeal.
