full_judgment:
3. Plaint case, in short, is that the suit land along with other land of CS Plot No. 158 originally belonged to one Abdul Kader and the record of rights were finally prepared and published in his name in CS khatian No. 4. Then, by a, registered deed of sale Abdul Kader transferred the entire land of said CS plot to Sharat Chandra Ghosh, Advocate. Sharat Chandra Ghosh possessed the land through 'Bargaders' Sheik Asanullah alias Munshi and Sheikh Mohammad for some time.Sharat Chandra Ghosh left a will giving the entire land of said plot to Premtosh Chandra Gosh and Bimal Chandra Chosh by a registered will dated 24 Ashar 1335 BS. The will was then duly probated on 13-7-35 in Probate Case No. 7 of 1934. 

 5. During survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, 66 decimals instead of 70 decimals was equally recorded in their names in SA khatian Nos. 197 and 196 respectively. At the time of RS survey, 33 decimals was similarly recorded in the name of each of them in RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225 respectively. 

 8. Defendant No. 14 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the plaint case. Its case, in short, is that the suit land along with other land belonged to Abdul Kader and CS record of rights was finally prepared and published in his name. Abdul Kader bequeathed the entire land of CS plot No. 158 by a registered deed of gift being 4133 dated 31-5-1917 to his three sons Sheikh Elahi Bux, Sheikh Abdul Karim and Sheikh Abdul Nabi and put them into possession. On 16-4-43 by way of family settlement Sheikh Elahi Bux and Sheikh Karim got the suit plot in their shares. Successive heirs of Sheik Elahi Bux and Sheik Abdul Karim, namely, Aziza Begum, Serajul Islam, Tehera Begum, Sonaban Bibi, Abdul Motaleb, Abdus Shahid and Abdul Hamid, jointly possessed the suit land along with other land by cultivation and growing fruits openly, publicly and adversely to the entire world. 

 11. On the party pleadings the following issues were finally settled: 

 14. He stated that the suit land was a part of CS plot No. 158 appertaining to CS khatian No.4. The plot comprised of 5.68 acres. The suit land was finally recorded and published in the name of Abdul Kader. By a deed being No. 351 dated 12-1-1921, Exhibit 1, Abdul Kader transferred the entire land of said CS plot No. 158 to one Sharat Chandra Ghosh, Advocate, Sharat Chandra Ghosh possessed the suit land through 'Bargaders' Sheik Ahsanullah Munshi and Sheikh Mohammad who gave a joint registered 'Barga kabuliyat' being deed No. 2810 dated 19-5-1924, Exhibit 2(ka) for a period of six years. Then, Sharat Chandra Ghosh left a will executed by him on 24 Ashar 1335 BS giving the entire land of said CS plot No. 158 to Premtosh Chandra Ghosh and Bimal Chandra Ghosh. After death of Sharat Chandra Ghosh, they on 19-7-1935 obtained a probate of the will in Probate Case NO.7 of 1934, Exhibits 3 and 6. 

 15. By a registered deed of sale being No. 4030 dated 24-9-1946 said Premtosh Chandra Ghosh and Bimal Chandra Ghosh transferred 70 decimals of land to Sheikh Hasenuddin. The original deed of Sheik Hasenuddin was adduced and marked Exhibit 4. After the death of Sheikh Hasenuddin, his heirs Samiruddin and others by two deeds being No. 6266 and 6268 dated 12-9-1955 transferred 70 decimals of land to Obaidul Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum and delivered possession. Original deeds were adduced and marked Exhibits 5 and 5(ka). During survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land was recorded equally in SA khatian Nos. 196 and 197 in the name of his father and mother, Exhibit 7 and 7(ka). Similarly, RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225, 7(kha) and 7(ga) were also prepared in the names of his parents. In the RS khatian a road was shown wrongly. Consequently, his father filed two written objections, which were accepted and mistake was corrected vide Exhibits 9 series. 

 38. As stated above, admittedly CS plot No. 158 appertaining to CS khatian No.4 including the suit land originally belonged to Abdul Kader and CS record of rights was finally prepared and published in his name. 

 39. It is the case of the plaintiff that Abdul Kader transferred the entire land of CS plot No. 158 to Sharat Chandra Ghosh, Advocate by a registered deed of sale being No. 351 dated 12-1-1921 and delivered possession. A certified copy of said document was adduced by the plaintiffs and marked Exhibit 2. Sharat Chandra Ghosh possessed the suit land for some time through 'Bargaders'. namely, Sheik Asanullah Munshi and Sheik Mohammad by executing registered 'Barga Kabuliyat' dated 19-5-1924. The plaintiffs adduced a certified copy of the Kabuliyat which was marked Exhibit 2(kha). Sharat Chandra Ghosh gave the suit land to Premtosh Ghosh and Bimal Chandra Ghosh by a registered deed of will executed on 24 Ashar 1335 BS. The will was duly proved on 13-11-1934 and probate granted thereon on 19-7-35 in Probate Case No.7 of 1934. To prove the will and probate, the plaintiffs adduced a certified copy of the will, Exhibit 6 and suit register of said Probate Case No. 7 of 1934, Exhibit 3. In the column, "order made and date" of the suit register, it was recorded that the will was proved on 13-11-1934 and probated on 13-7-1935. Premtosh Chandra Ghosh and Bimal Chandra then transferred 70 decimals of CS plot No. 158 to Hasenuddin by a registered deed of sale dated 24-9- 46. The plaintiff adduced the original deed, which was marked Exhibit 1. After death of Hasenuddin, his heirs Samiruddin and seven others by two registered deeds of sale dated 12-9-1955 transferred equally said 70' decimals of land to Obaidul Islam, original plaintiff and his wife Gulshan Begum. Those deeds were adduced and marked as Exhibit 5 and 5(ka). During survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 66 decimals instead of 70 decimals was equally recorded in the names of Obaidul. Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum in SA khatian Nos. 196 and 197 Exhibit 7 and 7(ka). During RS survey said land was again recorded as RS plot Nos. 1207, 1208 and 1209 in RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225 in their names Exhibit 7(kha) and 7(ga). The plaintiffs adduced rent receipts showing payment of rents, Exhibit 8 series and counterfoils evidencing possession through tenants, Exhibit 10 series. 

 49. We find that the suit land was already recorded in the names of original plaintiff Obaidul Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum during survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in plot Nos. 298/302 and 298/303 appertaining to SA khatian Nos. 196 and 197. Such record of rights was published some time in 1964. On the basis of such record of rights the plaintiff possessed the suit land exclusively on payment of rents on proper receipt Exhibit 8 series. Similarly, under the RS survey the suit land was again recorded in the names of Obaidul Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum in RS plot Nos. 1207, 1208 and 1209 appertaining to RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225 and RS record of rights was published in 1980s.

lawyer:
AF Hassan Ariff with Borhanuddin, Advocates — For the Appellant

full_judgment:
2. Plaint case briefly is this, certain lands owned by the plaintiffs along with the lands of others were requisitioned in LA Case No.138 of 1961-62 on 31-5-62 under the Town Improvement Act of 1953. Initially area of the lands requisitioned was 2760.00 acres, but subsequently in 1966 the area under requisition was reduced to 832.00 acres and consequently Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, was requested by Rajuk to derequisition the remaining requistioned lands and to order the owners concerned for refunding the compensation money already paid to them. In spite of the said position long thereafter Rajuk published a tender notice being No.3/-94-95 on 22-9-94 in the daily Inqilab inviting tender for filling up the lands left out of the requisition and for this plaintiffs were restrained to file the present suit. 

 8. Mr SR Pal, learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-respondents, submits that the RS Khatians have already been finally published recording the names of the plaintiffs as tenants under the Government in respect of the lands in question. This also indicates that the plaintiffs can invoke the doctrine of estoppel on the basis of the RS Khatians. 

 12. Relevant fact leading to the filing of the present First Miscellaneous Appeal is as follows: The respondent opposite party Nos. 1 to 6 as plaintiffs have instituted Title Suit No. 219 of 1994 in the Court of the 3rd Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, for declaration that as they have right, title, interest in the plaint schedule land, plaint schedule land is no longer included in the LA Case No. 138/61-62 and that the notification No. 3/94-95 dated 22-9-94 published in the Daily Inqilab inviting tender for earth filling is illegal and void. 

 13. The plaint case of the respondent Nos. 1 to 6, in short, is that land of CS Khatian Nos. 81, 370, 350, 401, 229, 391 and 362 in total about 12.64 acres of land in Mouza boar Sahara originally belonged to Atabuddin and Golapdi, sons of late Doulate Sheikh in 8 annas shares and the same was amicably partitioned between the brothers. The plaintiffs inherited 12.64 acres of land out of CS Khatian No. 350, 401, 229, 2192, 391 and 362. Both SA Khatian and last RS Khatian were also prepared in the name of the present plaintiffs. The aforesaid 12-64 acres of land belonging to the plaintiffs were requisitioned under the said LA Case No. 138/61-62 inclusive of total 2760 acres of land from 11 moujas including Mouza Joar Shahara. The plaintiffs in spite of said requisition are all along in physical possession of the said land by paying rents to the Government. As per decision of the Board of Trustees of the former DIT now RAJUK the Government served notice on 31-5-1962 for requisition of 2760 acres of land including the aforesaid 12-64 acres of land of the plaintiffs vide LA Case No. 138/61-62. The Deputy Commissioner. Dhaka fixed a preliminary compensation for the land at the rate of Taka 8,952.75 and Taka 10,288.19 respectively and paid small amount to the predecessor of the plaintiffs at the rate of Taka 4,580.00 and Taka 8,000.00 as against actual current rate of Taka 5 (five) lakh per katha by way of compensation. Subsequently the Board of Trustees of former DIT now RAJUK took the decision in the meeting held on 15-12-1965 to acquire only 832 acres of land out of the said 2760 acres of land as the implementation of the scheme for such a vast area was impracticable and accordingly, requested the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to release the rest of the land from requisition. Accordingly, the Ministry of land Administration directed the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 6-5-1966 to take steps for derequisition of the said excess land and to ask for refund of the compensation money. The predecessor of the plaintiffs received such notice of derequisition and refund on 6-9-1966 and wanted to refund the compensation money received by them but could not succeed. 

 14. In this background of the matter the plaintiffs asserted that their land was in fact derequisitioned and, as such, the notification published in the Daily Inquilab by the appellant i.e. Rajuk for earth filing of their lands was illegal and void. 

 18. Mr SR Pal, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents, on the other hand, contends that since the government decided to implement the development scheme covering an area of only 832 acres of land or so and also directed the owners of the land failling out side of the said 832 acres of land to refund the compensation money, if so received by them, such land falling outside of the said 832 acres of land stood derequisitioned and as such the impugned notification for earth filing of such land after about 30 years of requisition is illegal and without jurisdiction. Mr SR Pal also contends by producing a RS Khatian that the said khatian also shows that the plaintiffs are in possession of the same and, as such, the plaintiffs have good prima facie arguable case for injunction. 

 25. Learned Advocate for the appellant submitted that in the judgment dated 22-11-93 of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992 as upheld by the Appellate Division by its judgment dated 27-3-94 in Civil Petition Nos. 117-119/1994 it was held that the suit land is still under requisition and RAJUK may deal with the said land as it appears expedient to RAJUK and, as such, plaintiff''s prayers in the Title Suit No.218/1994 for declaration that suit land was not under requisition in LA Case No.138/61-62 and defendant No. 3 RAJUK''s tender notice for filling up the suit land was illegal and that the plaintiffs have title in the suit land are nothing but reagitating the self same question agitated in the aforesaid writ petition. He contended that in the writ petition the question as to whether the suit land was under requisition having been finally declined on merit plaintiffs cannot raise the self same question in the suit again and such claim is barred by the principle of res judicata and so the plaintiffs are not entitled to temporary injunction. He further submitted that under the provisions of section 93C of the Town Improvement Act plaintiffs suit challenging the requisition is wholly barred and on that ground also plaintiffs'' suit is not maintainable and, as such, trial Court was not justified in holding that the suit is maintainable and allowing plaintiffs'' prayer for temporary injunction. 

 42. It appears from the plaint that plaintiffs prayed for declaration of their title in the suit land by inheritance, declaration that the suit land is not included under the notice of requisition in LA Case No.138/61-62 and that tender notice issued by the defendant No.3 in the daily Inqilab to engage contractors for filling up the suit land is without jurisdiction and void in respect of the suit land. In the plaint plaintiffs alleged that their title in the suit land has been clouded by the defendants'' action in not releasing the suit land twenty years after issuing the de-requisition notice and by the tender notice published in the daily Inqilab on 22-9-94 for filling up the suit land. There is no allegation in the plaint that plaintiffs'' title to get compensation money in respect of the suit requisitioned and has been denied by the defendants. If the entire plaint is read it is clear that the plaintiffs having claimed that though their predecessor could not refund the compensation money in pursuance of a notice of de-requisition their land is not under requisition and, as such, they are entitled to declaration of their title in the suit land and further declaration that their land is not under requisition in the aforesaid Land Acquisition Case and, as such, defendant No. 3 cannot ask any contractor to fill up the suit land with earth.

full_judgment: 3. The case of the plaintiffs opposite parties herein is interalia that the original owner of the land mentioned in tic schedule below was one Ramjan Ali and that C .S Khatian No 23 was finally published in his name. The said Ramjan Ali died leaving behind two sons namely Gura Miah and Syed Ali and two daughters namely, Sabur Khatun and Sadar Nisa alias Khatuni as his legal heirs. That during the time of R. S operation the said two daughters of Ramjan Ali were at their husbands house for which their names could not be recorded in the R S Khatians. But in spite of that they were in joint possession with their brothers Syed Ali and Gura Miah and. that the said Sadar Nisa alias Khatuni, Syed Ali, Thanda Miah, Abul Khatun and Tambia Khatun sold out 2.00 acres of land to plaintiff No 1 for their legal necessity including the schedule land vide registered kabala dated 9. 5. 1966 and delivered possession thereof to him and since the date of purchase the plaintiff No 1 is in peaceful possession of the same by paying rents, revenues etc. to the Government. Then he filed a Mutation Case No 572/11 of 1967-68 before the Circle Officer Hathazari, Chittagong who ordered for mutation of his name in S A Record but subsequently it was lost. Similarly the plaintiff No 2 also purchased .80 acre of land vide Registered kabala deeds dated 23.1.1984 and the plaintiff No 3 purchased .20 acre of land vide Registered kabala deed dated 23.1.1984 from one Bazal Ahmed, Oli Ahmed, Kabir Ahmed, Thanda Meah, Abul Khatun, Saleh Ahmed and Nur Begum on payment of proper consideration money and since then they are in peaceful possession of their purchased lands including .15 acre of the schedule land on payment of rent, to the Government. That the names of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 were also recorded in the S.A Khatian through Mutation and the names of all the plaintiffs subsequently were recorded in present revisional survey khatian vide Appeal Case No 28876 of 1982. Out of the purchased lands of the plaintiff .30 acre as mentioned in the schedule has been acquired by the Government vide L. A Case No 128 of 1983-84 (Misc. Case No 2 of 1984-85) for Gas line which was in the possession of the plaintiffs and the compensation money for the said acquisition has been assessed at Tk. 188442/-and that the plaintiffs are entitled to get the said compensation money and accordingly they filed a petition to the Land Acquisition Officer for getting the compensation money. It appears that the original defendant Nos. 1 to 3 who also claimed to have purchased some land of the R. S Khatian from said Syed Ali and Gura Meah lodged a claim for the compensation money, besides some other groups of peoples have also applied for getting their alleged shares in the compensation money and the Land Acquisition Officer after hearing all the parties passed his order on 12.10.1985 and awarded compensation to only defendants 1 to 3 and hence the present suit by the plaintiffs.

lawyer:
SR Pal, Senior Advocate, instructed by Miah Abdul Gafur, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Appellants. 
Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, Senior Advocate, instructed by Serajur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Respondent Nos. 1-2.
Not Represented ------- Respondents 3-74.
parties:
Joynal Abedin and others ------- Defendant-Appellants
 Vs.
Mafizur Rahman & others ------- Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 10, 11, 13-15 contending inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no title and possession; that the suit for simple partition is not maintainable; that the suit property Nos. 1 and 2 originally belonged to Sadaruddin, father of Khalil Patwari and Jinnat Ali on the basis of kabuliyat dated 8th Jaistha 1288 BS; that the landlord auction sold the said holding for arrears of rent in Rent Execution Case No. 64 of 1905 and one Kalimuddin auction purchased the same and got delivery of possession through Court; that thereafter he sold the same to Khalil Patwari by kabala dated 17th Kartick 1312 BS; that thereafter the said Jinnat Ali took settlement of 12 gondas equivalent to '72 acres from Khalil Patwari by executing Kabuliyat dated 27th Ashar. 1320 BS; that the said properties of Jinnat Ali were subsequently auction purchased by the heirs of Khalil Patwari for arrears of rent and possessed the same by taking delivery of possession through Court; that thereafter the landlord auction purchased the entire lands of the said original jote in Rent Execution Case No. 222 of 1950 for arrears of rent impleading all the heirs of Khalil Patwari and Jinnat Ali; and the landlord took delivery of possession in the said property through Court; that thereafter the answering defendants. plaintiffs brother defendant No. 1 and Fazler Rahman predecessor of defendant Nos. 6-8 took fresh settlement from the auction purchaser landlord; that defendant No. 1 and Fazler Rahman took settlement of specified '86 acres of lands; that the plaintiffs have been residing in the settled lands of defendant No.1 and Fazler Rahman; that Jinnat Ali was never owner in the properties of Khatian No. 233 and the same belonged to Khalil Patwari; that Jinnat Ali was owner of '72 acres in the properties of Khatian No. 236 but he fraudulently recorded his name in Khatian No. 233 as 15 gondas owner and recorded more lands in excess of his '72 acres in under raiyati khatian No. 236; that both the khatians are wrong and that the plaintiffs are not owners of '24 acres as claimed by them. Hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The trial Court dismissed the suit after holding that whatever interest Jinnat Ali, the predecessor of the plaintiffs had was extinguished by Rent Execution Case Nos. 64 of 1905 and No. 222 of 1950. The trial Court considered the sale certificates Ext. A and A(l) of the two Rent Execution cases and the writ of delivery of possession Ext. B in respect of the Rent Execution Case No. 64 of 1905. The trial Court further held that simple suit for partition as framed is not maintainable. 

 5. The lower appellate Court reversed the judgment of the trial Court after holding that on the face of CS Khatian Ext. 1 and 1 (a) finally published between 1913-16, bearing the name of Jinnat Ali, as the owner of the suit land, the alleged auction sale of the same in Rent Execution Case No. 64 of 1905 and the exhibits in support thereof are of no relevance and only indicate at its best that the alleged sale was a paper transaction. The lower appellate Court further held that even if there was any auction sale in paper the owners of the properties did not part with their possession and they actually possessed during the last CS operation and that the defendants having failed to produce any writ of delivery of possession about their alleged Rent Execution Case No. 222 of 1950 the interest of Jinnat Ali was not extinguished and Jinnat Ali had subsisting interest in the disputed property and consequently decreed the suit. The lower appellate Court accepted the correctness of the CS khatian and their presumptive value on the face of the documentary evidences adduced by the defendants to prove the auction sale and subsequent delivery of possession. 

 7. Leave was granted to consider whether the High Court Division misread the sale certificates Ext. A, A(l) and the writ of delivery of possession Ext. B and wrongly held that the interest of Jinnat Ali was not extinguished for not impleading all the co-sharer landlords in the rent suit and rent execution cases overlooking that Rajkishore not Mathura Mohan was landlord at the time of auction held in Rent Execution Case No. 64 or 1905 and other co-sharers landlords were impleaded by Mathura in Rent Execution Case No. 222 of 1950 as proforma defendant-judgment-debtor Nos. 8-13 and had wrongly decreed the suit and that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division grossly failed to consider the question of defect of parties in the Rent suit and Rent Execution case when Jinnat Ali the judgment-debtor himself acknowledged the auction sale by subsequently taking settlement of a part of the land from the auction purchaser by kabuliyats Ext. D and D(l) which were not at all considered by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division on misconception of law and fact 

 8. It appears that the kabuliyats Ext. D series were filed before the trial Court and those were not wrongly marked as exhibits. Consequently, at an earlier point of time the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division remanded the case to the lower appellate Court and those were marked exhibits without any objection by the parties. From the order of the lower appellate Court dated 9.6.83, it appears that those documents were filed by the defendants as per Firisti with a petition for accepting those in evidence and those were admitted in evidence without any objection from either side. Thereafter the appeal was heard in 1985 and in disposing of the appeal we find that the lower appellate Court did not say a word with regard to these kabuliyats nor had taken those into consideration. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division also on an erroneous view of the law left these vital documents out of consideration by holding that the certified copies of the kabuliyats were filed without calling for the original copies of the kabuliyats. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division on a wrong consideration of section 66 of the Evidence Act left those out of consideration as the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was of the opinion that those documents were not admissible in evidence as the originals were not called for. Mr. SR Pal, learned Advocate appearing for the defendant appellants rightly argued that the documents having been filed and marked Exhibit without any objection the question of admissibility of those documents cannot be raised at a subsequent point of time and the courts below including the leaned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted wrongly in not considering these kabuliyats Ext. D series and failed to consider the effect of these kabuliyats in the instant case. The learned Advocate in support of his argument has also cited the case of Abdullah and 3 others Vs. Abdul Karim and others reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205. In that decision it has been held that objection as to formal proof of a document is to be taken at the earliest point of time. In the present case, the document was admitted in evidence without any objection from either side in the year 1983. As a matter of fact the appeal came up for hearing in 1985 after a lapse of 2 years. Nobody raised the question of formal proof of those kabuliyats and those were admitted in evidence without objection. This being the position, the kabuliyats, exhibit D series were admissible in evidence and the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted wrongly in not considering those kabuliyats. Herein, we may mention that the kabuliyat by Jinnat Ali in favour of Khalil Patwari marked Ext. D and D(1) by which he took settlement of  70 acres of land admitted the auction and by the kabuliyats marked Ext. D(2) to D(8) some of the defendants who were heirs of Khalil Patwary and some other defendants who were heirs of Jinnat Ali took settlement of the entire suit land from the auction purchaser landlords. From the Kabuliyat Ext D(2) some of heirs of Jinnat Ali and by kabuliyat Ext. D(3) the names of plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were mentioned as executants and beneficiaries though only defendant No. 1 eldest brother of plaintiff No. 1 and defendant No.2 executed the same and as such they as heirs of Jinnat Ali admitted the auction purchase of the suit property by the landlord-recipient of the kabuliyat in Rent Execution Case No. 222 of 1950. Thus, it can be safely said that non-consideration of these vital documents namely, the certified copies of the kabuliyats which were admitted into evidence without objection had materially affected the decision in the present case. 

 9. It may further be mentioned that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division wrongly held that all the co-sharer landlords were not made parties in the rent suit. It may be pointed out that from exhibit 'A' series, sale Certificates, Rajkishore was the landlord at the time of auction sale held in Rent Execution Case No. 64 of 1905 and Mathura was not the landlord and in Rent Execution Case No. 222 of 1950 Mathura was the landlord. In the second auction sale possession was taken by landlord Mathura and the heirs of Jinnat Ali granted kabuliyat in favour of Mathura which shows that Mathura was in possession. Thus, without considering these documents the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division wrongly held that those two rent suits were filed by Mathura and other landlords have not filed any rent suit. Thus, non-consideration of these documents have resulted in an erroneous finding by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division that Mathura Mohan has not filed the Rent suit impleading the other co-sharers landlord as parties to the suit.

Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Ministry of Land, Bangladesh Secretariat, Shahbag, Dhaka and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why inclusion of SA Plot No. 14 in SA Khatian No. 81 measuring 34 decimals of land in Mouza-Panchuria, JL No. 92 under Police Station-Gopalganj Sadar, District-Gopalganj in the "ka" schedule of vested property at serial No. 214/1 which has been published on 264-2012 in Bangladesh Gazette under section 9(1) of the "অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ (সংশোধিত ২০১১)” (Annexure-E), should not be declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect, and as to why the respondents should not be directed to release the SA Plot No. 14 from SA Khatian No. 81 measuring 34 decimals of land in Mouza-Panchuria, JL No. 92 under Police Station-Gopalganj Sadar, District-Gopalganj from the "Ka" schedule of vested property what they are required by law to do and/or pass such other or further order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 2. The background facts of the case as presented by the petitioners leading to issuance of the Rule in short are that the schedule land was originally owned by Sree Mahima Charan Kar, son of Gopal Charan Kar and SA Khatian No. 68 was published in his name. Later, his son Nitynanda Kar inherited the said property and sold it to Adittya Nath Biswas, predecessor of the petitioners, vide a registered sale deed, dated 17-1-1958. Thereafter SA Khatian No. 81 containing two plots of land including the schedule property was published in the name of Adittya Nath Biswas and two others. Then SA Khatian No. 83, containing only the schedule property was published in the sole name of Adittya Nath Biswas. Upon death of Adittya Nath Biswas, SA Khatian No. 83 was published in the name of all his four sons. Subsequently BRS Khatian No. 51 and 74 were published in the name of the petitioners. Since purchase of the schedule property, Adittya Nath Biswas and his heirs have been paying regular land tax and other government dues in their names till the year 2016. Thereafter, upon publication of the BRS records, when the petitioners went to pay land tax in 2019, land office refused to accept land tax from the petitioners on the plea that -the said property has been listed as a vested property. In the meantime, limitation period for filing a regular suit before the Tribunal has passed and being compelled, the petitioners preferred this writ petition and obtained Rule. 

 3. Mr. Tapan Kumar Biswas, along with Mr. Mohammad Najmul Huda and Mr. Sukumar Biswas, learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners placed the writ petition and supplementary affidavit. He submits that the predecessor of the petitioners Sree Adittya Nath Biswas purchased the schedule property, from Sree Nittyananda Kar, son of Mahima Charan Kar, the original owner of the said land which was recorded in his name under RS Khatian No. 68. Purchase was done vide, registered sale deed No. 665, dated 17-1-1958. Thereafter, SA Khatian No. 81 was published in the name of Nittyananda Kar, Adittya Nath Biswas and Surendra Nath Basu. Subsequently SA Khatian No. 83 was published in the sole name of Adittya Nath Biswas. Upon death of said Adittya Nath Biswas, SA Khatian No. 83 (Annexure-B-2) was published in the name of all his four sons (i) Nakul Chandra Biswas; (ii) Gopinath Biswas; (iii) Gopal Chandra Biswas: (iv) Mohadev Biswas. Thereafter, BRS Khatian No. 51 and 74 (Annexure-C and C-1) were prepared and published in the name of the petitioners. 

 4. He then submits that since purchase of the schedule property in the year 1958, petitioners and their predecessors have been paying the land tax and other government dues in their own names. Lastly they paid the land tax in 2016 (Annexure-D-3) in their own names and after publication of the BRS khatian when the petitioners went to pay the land tax, concerned officer of the land office refused to accept land tax from them. Only then the petitioners came to know that their property has been included in the "Ka" list of the vested properties under serial No. 214/1. 

 5. Mr. Bisixas submits that the petitioners have been possessing and enjoying the schedule land through inheritance from their predecessor who purchased the schedule land from the rightful owner of the same on 17-1-1958 and since then they have continuously mutated their names in the land records regarding the schedule property and paid land tax till 2016. But, the respondents have included the said land in the list of vested properties without any lawful reason. SA Khatian No. 83 was correctly prepared and published in the name of the predecessors of the petitioners, subsequently BRS records were also published in the name of the petitioners. Therefore, including the schedule property in the "Ka" list of the vested properties is arbitrary and illegal. 

 6. Then he submits that apart from the name of the predecessor of the petitioners, SA Khatian No. 81 contained two other names, namely Nityananda Karr and Surendra Nath Basu. Said Khatian included two plots; plot No. 14 consisting 34 decimals and plot No. 156 consisting of 35 decimals of land. Khatian No. 81 included a comment being "vinno kali/ different ink" shown against the name of Adittya Nath Biswas. Subsequently. when SA Khatian No. 83 was published in the sole name of Aditta nath Biswas, it contained only plot No. 14, consisting 34 decimals of land. Later on when said khatian was published in the names of four sons of Aditta Nath Biswas, it also contained only plot No. 14, consisting of 34 decimals of land. 

 8. He further submits that the schedule property has been included in the "Ka" list of the vested properties lists at serial No. 214/1 (Annexure-E) in the gazette. But, the said list did not publish the names of the owners and the present plot number and khatian number, which is violation of the provision of Clause 9 of the, Arpita Sompatti Prottarpan Ain, 2001 and hence it is not sustainable under the law. 

 11. Mr. Islam submits that the disputed land under SA Khatian No. 81 contains two plots of land being plot No. 14 and 156 and the said khatian was published in the name of Nittyananda Kar, son of Mahima Charan Kar, Adittya Nath Biswas, son of Gurucharan Biswas and Surendra Nath Basu, son of Rajanikanta Basu. Nittyananda Kar left for India during the war between India and Pakistan in 1965 and never returned, hence said khatian has been enlisted in the "Ka" list of the vested properties under serial No. 214/1 and the gazette was published on 24-4-2012 under section 9 of the Aipita Sompatti Prottarpan Ain, 2001 as amended in 2010. 

 13. Mr. Islam then submits that the comment in "vinno kali/ different ink" has been shown in the SA Khatian No. 81 against the name of Adittya Nath Biswas, but this court is not in a position to take evidence as to whether "vinno kali/ different ink" was actually used in Khatian No. 81 or not. Hence, as this court does not have the jurisdiction to determine the factual aspect of this case, the Rule issued in this matter should be discharged. 

 14. Then he submits that the name of the predecessor of the petitioners was wrongly published in SA Khatian No. 83. SA Plot No. 14 consists of 34 decimals of land and said plot number is also included SA Khatian No. 81. Since Nittyananda Kar has left the country during the 1965 war and SA Khatian No.-81 being published in his name have rightly been included in the list of vested properties, therefore instant Rule should be discharged. 81 being published in his name have rightly been included in the list of vested properties, therefore instant Rule should be discharged. 

 17. It appears from the record that the gazette notification, dated 24-4-2012 includes the schedule property in the "Ka" list at serial No. 214/1 under VP Case No. X11/5/1464/68-69 showing that the said property has been under the possession of the Government since 13-2-1969, but this publication does not include the name of the owner of SA Khatian No.81 containing SA plot No. 14 and 156 measuring in total 59 decimals of land (34 decimals in plot No. 14 and 35 decimals in plot No. 156). 

 18. We have seen from the presented documents that since purchasing the land of plot No. 14, consisting 34 decimals by Adittya Nath Biswas a separate Khatian being No. 83 was prepared and published by including plot No. 14, consisting 34 decimals of land (whole land of the said plot). Since a new khatian has been published in the name of the new owner and as the respondents jailed to raise any plausible allegation of illegality regarding publication of the same, Khatian No. 83 shall supersede the Khatian No. 81. 

 26. Respondents are directed hereby to exclude the schedule property from the "Ka" list published in the Bangladesh Gazette, dated 26-4-2012 (Annexure-E) within 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of this judgment.

3. Facts leading, to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that, the suit plot No.638 and 639 along with on non suited plot No.643 measuring 39 decimals of land originally belonged to Samina Bibi which was finally published in her name in Cadastral Survey (in short, C.S.) Khatian and that the said Samena Bibi died leaving behind her only daughter Amena Khatun and thereafter Amena Khatun died leaving behind her daughter Malekernesa alias Maleka. While Maleka was owning and possessing the said plots, she transferred the entire land of plot no.643 by executing and registering deed of sale no.3219 dated 26.04.62 and 07 decimals of land from the suit plots by  executing and registering another deed of sale bearing no.4967 dated 6.12.1972 to the plaintiff no.4 Abdul Sobhan alias Sobhan Miah. After purchase he mutated his name and got Jama Separated in Separation Case No.224/83-84 by creating a separate Khatian No.982 and took a loan from the Janata Bank, Brahmanbaria Branch by mortgaging the said 07 decimals of land. Thereafter, Maleka Begum died leaving behind one son Abdul Hossain, father of plaintiff No. 5, who died leaving behind plaintiff nos.3-5 as his sons and daughter and thus the plaintiff nos.1-4 became the owners of 27 decimals of land in the suit plot by way of purchase and by inheritance. That in State Acquisition (in short, S.A.) operation, the suit property along with the property of plot no.643 has been  wrongly recorded in the name of one Aderjaman and other, predecessors of the defendants in khatian no.117. The plaintiff learnt about the wrong record in the S.A. Khatian on the basis of so-called partition suit no.172 of 1929. The defendant No.5 with help of other defendants forcibly entered into the plot no.638 on 30.09.96 and constructed two Dochala tin shade and 3 Chouchala tin shade house defying the objection raised by plaintiff no.3. 

 4. The defendant No.3 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and that the suit plot nos.638 and 639 along with non-suited plot no.643 measuring an area of 39 decimals of land belonged to Samina Bibi and  her name was rightly recorded in C.S. Khatian. Samina Bibi subsequently defaulted to pay rents and the Talukder was going to file a suit for realization of rent then Samina Bibi executed Istafanama deed dated 06.06.1920 and surrendered the property in favour of the landlord who settled the property to Munshi Mia, son of Nawaj Ali on 10.09.1921 and thus Munshi Mia became the sole owner of the land of the said 3 plots and has been possessing of the said land and prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 10. Md. N.K. Saha, the learned Senior Counsel  appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in disturbing the findings of facts arrived at by both the Courts below and on misreading of the evidence on record committed an error of law in holding that the plaintiffs did not mention the date of cause of action and the date of dispossession and also gave perverse finding upon non-consideration of the findings of facts recorded by the lower Appellate Court. He next submits that the High Court Division made the Rule absolute in finding that both the Courts below specially the Appellate Court being the last Court of facts misread the evidence on record that the plaintiff did not mentioned the date of cause of action and the date of dispossession and  also gave perverse finding in failing to consider that neither the Trail Court not the lower Appellate Court found that the plaintiffs have not mentioned the date of cause of action and date of dispossession, rather, both the Courts below found that the plaintiffs failed to prove the date of cause of action and date of dispossession, as such, the observation made by the High Court Division is perverse which is liable to be set aside. He finally submits that the Trial Court found that the plaintiff did not adduce any direct witness to prove alleged dispossession and the Appellate Court affirmed those findings but the High Court Division neither reversed those finding arrive at on consideration of material evidence on record nor gave any independent finding regarding to  the plaintiffs’ title, date of knowledge about S.A. Plot No.117, proof of alleged dispossession, limitation and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed.

full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel, J: On an application under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inclusion of the case property measuring an area of 39 decimals of land out of SA Plot No.1058 corresponding to RS Plot No.679 appertaining to SA Khatian No.147 and RS Khatian No.42 of Mouza Dakkingaon, Police Station Shabujbagh, Dhaka at serial No.7 in 'Ka' schedule of vested properties published in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 2-5-2012 (Annexure-'H' to the writ petition) should not be declared to be without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and why the respondents should not be directed to release the case property from "Ka" schedule of vested property in favour of the petitioners and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule as set out in the writ petition, in short, are that CS Khatian No.118 of Mouza-Dakkhingaon under Police Station-Sabek Keraniganj, thereafter Tejgaon and at present-Sabujbag within District-Dhaka was prepared and published in the names of Brindaban Koibartta and Tufani Koibartta, both sons of Guru Proshad. In that khatian, 104 decimals of land were recorded under CS Plot No.1058 wherein they were the owners in equal shares. The said Tufani Koibartta died leaving behind his only son Pagol Nath Das who obtained 52 decimals of land in CS Plot No.1058 appertaining to CS Khatian No.118 of the aforesaid Mouza by way of inheritance from his deceased father. Thereafter, Pagol Nath Das sold out the said 52 decimals of land in favour of Abdus Samad Ahmed, son of Moulavi Tasir Uddin Ahmed vide registered sale deed being No.5763, dated 22-5-1957. Accordingly, SA Khatian No.147 covering 52 decimals of land in SA Plot No.1058 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad. During RS survey, RS Khatian No.42 covering 48 decimals of land in RS Plot No.679 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad Ahmed. 

 3. Thereafter, Abdus Samad Ahmed sold out the said 52 decimals of land in favour of Rai Raman Mitra vide registered sale deed being No.1897, dated 17-1-1978. Out of the said 52 decimals of land, Rai Raman Mitra sold out 13 decimals of land to the instant petitioner No.1, Md Ilias Hossain vide registered sale deed being No.42072, dated 1-12-1978, (Annexure-B(i) of the writ petition). The said Rai Raman Mitra also sold out 26 decimals of land in favour of Mosammat Jahanara Begum, mother of the petitioner Nos.2-5 vide registered sale deed being No.42148, dated 1-12-1978, (Annexure-B(ii) of the writ petition). Thereafter, the petitioner No.I mutated his name in respect of 13.82 decimals of land vide Mutation Case No.5070 P-1/05, dated 12-5-2005. The said Mosammat Jahanara Begum out of her 26 decimals of land, sold out 5.61 decimals of land in favour of the petitioner Nos.6- 7 vide registered sale deed being No.3741, dated 28-6-1995, then 4.49 decimals of land in favour of the petitioner Nos.8-9 vide registered sale deed being No.3742, dated 28-6-1995 and 4.95 decimals of land in favour of Noorjahan Begum, mother of the petitioner Nos.10-12 vide registered sale deed being No.6113, dated 20-6-1988, (Annexure-C,C(i) and C(ii) of the writ petition). Thereafter, during Mohanagar Jarip, Mohanagar Khatian covering the case land were prepared and published in the names of the petitioner No.1, mother of the petitioner Nos.2-5, petitioner Nos.6-7, petitioner Nos.8-9 and mother of the petitioner Nos.10-12 accordingly without any objection from any quarter. The petitioner No.1 sold out 5.85 decimals of land in favour of the petitioner Nos.13-14 vide registered sale deed being No.5320, dated 14-7-2008, (Annexure-E & E(i) of the writ petition) and accordingly, they have mutated the said land in their respective names. The petitioner Nos.2-5 obtained 7.26 decimals of land by way of inheritance from their deceased mother Jahanara Begum and they have mutated the said land in their names (Annexure-F of the writ petition). The petitioners are possessing their 39 decimals of land for a long time since their respective date of purchase by erecting residential houses on the land. They have paid up to date revenue rent as per the latest Mohanagar khatian. 

 4. On the 1st week of January, 2016 the petitioner No.1 went to the office of the respondent No.4, Tohsilder, Shabujbagh Tohshil Office for payment of his revenue rent for the year of 1422 BS, but the respondent No.4 refused to accept the rent on the ground that the land has been included in the list of vested property as "Ka" schedule land. Thereafter, on scrutiny, the petitioners found that SA Plot No.1058 corresponding to RS Plot No.679 covering their land has been included in the list of vested property, published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 2-5-2012 (Annexure-H of the writ petition). The property of the petitioners was vested to the Government in connection with VP Case No.523 of 1979. The petitioners came to know about the VP list on the 1st week of the January, 2016 and in the meantime, statutory period of limitation to apply before the Arpito Sampatti Prottorpan Tribunal, which was 31-12-2013 as per section 10 of the "অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১" elapsed. Being aggrieved by the inclusion of the said land of the petitioners at serial No. 7 in the list of 'Ka' schedule vested property Gazette, published on 2-5-2012, the petitioners finding no other alternative efficacious remedy filed the instant writ petition before this Hon'ble Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. He further submits that on a perusal of the annexure-H, it is found that the owner of the property in question was Joy Durga Bewa and others, but on perusal of the documents annexed herewith, it is apparent that never the property was recorded in the name of Joy Durga Bewa or others at any point of time, rather, SA, RS and latest Mohanagar Khatian has been prepared in the name of the present petitioners and their vendor or predecessor Abdus Samad. Hence, inclusion of the property in the 'Ka' schedule is not in accordance with law. 

 9. He finally submits that after 1974, the inclusion of the petitioners property in the list of vested property is illegal and also violative of Article 42 of the Constitution of Peoples Republic of Bangladesh. The petitioners can come directly to the High Court Division for protection of their right to property guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution of Peoples Republic of Bangladesh. Therefore, the writ petition is maintainable. To fortify his submissions, he relied upon the following decisions, which are as follows:- 

 11. Per Contra, Mr Amit Das Gupta, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka by filing an affidavit-in-¬opposition submits that the Authority rightly and lawfully included the case property in the vested property list, published by Gazette notification dated 2-5-2012. He submits that the petitioners were fully aware about the Gazette notification and without going to the proper forum, being the Arpito Shampotti Tribunal for releasing their property, they filed the instant writ petition. They have no scope to prefer this writ petition as per the existing law of the land. As such, the instant writ petition is not maintainable, since they have alternative remedy. 

 12. He submits that the list of returnable property was prepared in order to return the property enlisted as vested property to the original owners, according to the Act of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১. Accordingly, on 2-5-2012, the Gazette was published following all the legal formalities. 

 13. He next submits that the mutation does not establish any right and title over any property, rather, mutation is normally allowed to realize Government Revenue. At the time of mutation of RS Khatian, the vested property Gazette notification was not published, as a result mutation Khatian was prepared in absence of the related vested property list. The property has been declared as vested property and leased out vide VP Case No.523 of 1979 and therefore, the purchase of the vested property by the petitioners is not proper as per law. 

 14. He finally submits that inclusion of the property in the 'Ka' schedule list of the vested property has been made following all the legal formalities, and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 16. It appears that the main cause to file this writ petition is the Gazette notification dated 2-5- 2012 (Annexure-H) wherein the petitioners property was included at serial No.7 as vested property. It appears from the record that the property in question that is CS Khatian No.118 of Mouza-Dakkhingaon under Police Station-Sabek Keraniganj, thereafter Tejgaon, at present¬Sabujbag within District-Dhaka was prepared and published in the names of Brindaban Koibartta and Tufani Koibartta, both sons of Guru Proshad. In that khatian, 104 decimals of land were recorded under CS Plot No.1058, as evidenced from the annexure-X of the writ petition. Thereafter, Tufani Koibartta died leaving behind his only son Pagol Nath Das who obtained 52 decimals of land in the CS Khatian No.118 of the aforesaid Mouza by way of inheritance from his deceased father and the said Pagol Nath Das sold out the said 52 decimals of land in favour of Abdus Samad Ahmed vide registered sale deed being No.5763, dated. 22-5-1957 (Annexure-Y of the writ petition). It appears that before SA survey, the said Abdus Samad Ahmed purchased 52 decimals of land and accordingly, SA Khatian No.147 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad Ahmed. Thereafter, during RS survey, RS Khatian No.42 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad Ahmed and 48 decimals of land was recorded in RS Plot No.679 of the said Khatian. Thereafter, Abdus Samad Ahmed sold out 52 decimals of land in favour of one Rai Raman Mitra vide registered sale deed No.1897, dated 17-1-1978. Subsequently, the present petitioners obtained 39 decimals of land out of said 52 decimals of land by way of purchase. It is clear from the record that at the relevant time of inclusion of the case land as vested property, the case land actually belonged to Abdus Samad Ahmed and hence the question of his whereabouts being unknown did not arise at all. Therefore, there is no basis to treat the case land as vested property. 

 18. Now, in respect to the issue of maintain¬ability of the present writ petition, it appears from the record that the Government has accepted rent from the petitioners up to 1421 BS and since their respective date of purchase, the petitioners are possessing the land by erecting residential houses on payment of revenue rent as per the latest Mohanagar Khatian as evidenced from annexures G to G (iv) respectively of the writ petition. Moreover, the possession of the petitioners has not been disturbed from any quarter in any way. Therefore, it is natural that they had no knowledge about their land being enlisted as vested property until the office of the respondent No.4 refused to accept the rent for the year of 1422 BS. Admittedly, by this time, the last date for filing a suit before the "অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১” expired. As such, they have no other alternative remedy other than filing this writ petition. 

 23. In light of the above discussions, we are of the view that the case property is not a vested property, rather it has been included in the list of vested property by violating the provision of the law. Therefore, the inclusion of the property in the schedule 'Ka' of the vested property list, published in the Gazette notification dated 2-5¬2012, (Annexure-H) is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 26. The respondents are hereby directed to exclude the case property from `Ka' schedule of the vested property list published in Bangla-desh Gazette dated 2-5-2012 through a fresh Gazette notification within 60 (sixty) days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order positively.

59. P.W.1 Md. Mahbub Alam Howlader stated that after the crack down by the Pak occupation army on the night following 25th March, 1971, as per direction of Sheikh Muzibur Rahman the people organized Mukti Bahini for fighting against the tyrant regime and started guerrilla fighting and sometimes thereafter, the anti-liberation forces like Sekandar Ali Sikder, Danesh Ali Molla, Moslem Uddin Moulana, Azahar Ali Talukder, Delwar Hossain Sayedee, Mohsin, A. Karim, Habibur Rahman Munshi, Sobhan Moulana, Hakim Kari and others formed Shanti Committee at Parerhat. Besides them, Madrasha students, the anti- liberation activists formed Razakars force and they started working as collaborators of Pak army. In the first part of May, 1971, Pak army came to Pirojpur and as Delwar Hossain Sayedee could speak Urdu fluently worked as interpreter of captain Ejaz and entered to Parerhat with the Pak occupation army. He stated that after looting the shops of Makhon Lal Saha, Modan Saha, they came to Baduria and Chitolia villages and looted the houses of Manik Posari and others and destroyed their houses by fire and that though Sekandar Ali and Danesh Ali Molla took leading part, Delwar Hossain Sayedee having proficiency in Urdu speaking developed closeness with captain Ezaj and actively participated in those atrocities. In course of cross-examination, he reaffirmed his claim made in chief and stated that Delwar Hossain Sayedee was present at Parerhat and denied the defence suggestion that Sayedee was not involved in the looting and arson of the houses of Manik Posari. The defence could not bring anything by cross-examining him to discredit his testimony. 

 61. Md. Mostafa Howlader (P.W.8) corroborated P.Ws.1 and 4 as regards the formation of Peace Committee with the appellant in Parerhat area. He also stated regarding the incident of destruction caused to the houses of Nuru Khan by the local Razakars with the help of Ayub. By pointing fingers at Delwar Hossain Sayedee he stated that Sayedee identified the house of Nuru Khan. In course of cross-examination, he reaffirmed his statement in chief stating that before 8th May, 1971, none damaged Saiz Uddin Posari's houses. This suggestion indicated that the defence has also admitted the destroy of the houses of Saiz Uddin Posari by fire but according to the defence, the houses were damaged before 8th May, 1971. The defence failed to bring anything to show that the houses were destroyed before 8th May, 1971. It did not adduce any evidence that the incident took place prior to 8th May. He reaffirmed his statement in a reply to another query that he saw the incidents of setting fire from a distance of about 200/300 yards. He specifically mentioned the distance between the place where he was standing and the incident houses, which according to him was the bank of the canal. He denied the defence suggestion that Delwar Hossain Sayedee was not present at Parerhat on 4 or 5 May. He was thoroughly cross-examined by the defence but failed to shake his testimony in any manner. The inconsistencies which defence tried to establish were trifling in nature. 

 64. Their statements were recorded by the investigation officer Md. Helal Uddin (P.W.28). This witness stated that after the examination of some witnesses, the production of the remaining witnesses before the Tribunal was not possible due to time restraint and threat given to them.  119. It is true that P.Ws.1, 3 and 4 made general statements about the rape of Hindu women by the army in collaboration with the local Razakars. It is, however, a historical fact that during the liberation struggle period the Pak Army being assisted by the Razakars tortured the women particularly Hindu women indiscriminately. Anthony Mascarenhas in the journal 'The Guardian' has reported the barbaric acts of violation to girls by the occupation forces as mentioned earlier. This fact has been admitted by D.Ws.3, 14 and 16. D.W.3 in his chief volunteered that Gouranga Saha complained that Sayedee took his sisters at the army camp where they were ravished. He was deposing incident of 1971 as would appear from the statement that in 1971, Gouranga Saha told him that Delwar Hossain Sayedee was involved in abducting his sisters and handing them over to army who were then raped. Sub-section (3) of section 19 empowers the Tribunal to take judicial notice of facts of common knowledge. 

 134. This Division in the case of Abdul Quader Mollah held since the provisions of Code of Criminal Procedure are not applicable to the trials before the Tribunal constituted under Act of 1973, the examination of a witness by the investigation officer in course of investigation may be either orally or in writing. As there is nothing in the Rules guiding the procedure and the manner of use of earlier statement of a witness in the trial, in view of sub-rule (ii) of Rule 53, the contradiction can only be drawn from the statements made by a witness in his examination-in-chief and not with respect to a statement made to the investigation officer. In the absence of any Rules guiding the procedure for recording statement of a witness, normally the investigating officers examine the witnesses sometimes in a slip shod manner and sometimes at his whims. Therefore, the defence is not legally entitled to take contradiction of the statement of a witness with his earlier statement made to the investigation officer in accordance with section 145 of the Evidence Act. 

 135. Reading section 19(2) and rule 53(ii) of the Rules together, one may come to a conclusion that can be arrived that a statement of a witness recorded by an investigation officer can be admitted in evidence if his presence before the Tribunal cannot be procured or that he is not alive, otherwise not. Contradicting the statement of a witness can be drawn subject to the condition that it must be strictly limited to the subject-matter of the examination- in-chief only. Even without taking contradiction, the veracity of a witness can be impeached by extracting his knowledge about the subject on which he has deposed, his motives to depose in the case, his interest, his inclination, his means of obtaining a correct facts to which he deposes, the manner in which he has used those means, his powers of discerning facts in the first instance, his capacity for retaining and describing them etc. The witness may also be cross-examined for the discovery of truth for the purpose of ascertaining his credibility. 

 136. It is to be remembered that the object of cross-examination is to bring out desirable facts of the case modifying the examination-in-chief and to impeach the credit of the witness. The other object of cross-examination is to bring out facts which go to diminish or impeach the trustworthiness of the witness. In examination-in-chief a witness discloses only a part of the necessary facts, not discloses a part of the necessary facts, not merely because the witness is a partisan of the party calling him but also his evidence is given only by way of answers to specific questions, and the prosecuting counsel producing him usually calls for nothing but the facts favourable to his party. Cross-examination, then has for its utility, the extraction of the remaining qualifying circumstances of the testimony given by the witness in his examination-in-chief. Learned Attorney General argued that the expressions "the party shall be at liberty to cross-examine such witness on his credibility" used in sub-rule (ii) of Rule 53 are sufficient to infer that the Rules have debarred `-the Tribunal to take into consideration the .inconsistent statements of any witness made in course of investigation to the investigation officer. Therefore, there is no scope under the rules of evidence to infer contradiction of the statements of the witnesses with what they have stated to the investigation officer. The basic principles of interpretation of statutes is that laws should be construed to carry out the intention of the legislature. The function of the court is to interpete a statute according to its intent. 

 143. Similarly, in our view the prosecutor appears to be a novice law officer, who has no elementary knowledge in conducting a case on behalf of the prosecution and also the method of examination-in-chief of a witness. There are serious loopholes in the way the case has been conducted and he has not endeavoured to rectify those defects. Either intentionally or due to lack of adequate knowledge, he has treated the case callously. If he has no elementary knowledge to conduct such a serious case, he should not have taken the responsibility of the case. The Chief Prosecutor also cannot avoid the responsibility in this regard. If he cannot supervise the cases there is no reason for him to occupy the office. The prosecution team should not gamble with the blood of martyrs. It is the duty of the prosecuting counsel to ask a witness questions carefully. He should keep in mind that a witness should not be questioned without an object or without being able to connect that object with the case. We are shocked by the manner in which the cases like this one are handled by them.
